qJYdZFEdWI.one_liner: Learns nested component masks with a sigmoid top-k operator and random k, ranking model components by attribution score.
qJYdZFEdWI.problem: Existing attribution of language model outputs to internal computations, via causal interventions, gradients, or learnable masks, is infeasibly expensive or fails to identify causally important components.
qJYdZFEdWI.method: Matryoshka Attribution (MAttr) frames attribution as finding nested subsets of internal components that minimize a downstream loss, parametrizing the mask with a differentiable sigmoid top-k operator and randomizing k during training so one run yields a learned ordering over all sparsities. It can also be trained with reinforcement learning to identify weight changes responsible for downstream behaviors in LLM finetuning.
qJYdZFEdWI.key_idea: Supervise a differentiable sigmoid top-k mask at randomly sampled sparsities k, so one training run learns a nested ordering of components by attribution score.
qJYdZFEdWI.evidence: The Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark (MIB) and an extended MIB+ across several models, tasks, and component types, plus a refusal-removal study on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct.
qJYdZFEdWI.claimed_gains: Achieves number 1 on the official MIB leaderboard, and restoring 1% of Llama 3.1 8B Instruct's weights to their base model state is sufficient to remove refusals while maintaining capabilities.
qJYdZFEdWI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree MAttr improves over a wide array of baselines on MIB's circuit performance ratio (CPR), often by a wide margin, with a simple method that yields circuits at all sparsity levels in one run.
qJYdZFEdWI.main_concern: The gains rest on the CPR metric, while MAttr is reported behind several baselines on circuit-model distance (CMD) and close to Integrated Gradients on compactness, which the paper does not discuss.

AsDkLi7mAk.one_liner: Differentiable surrogate of global Average Precision ranking all query-candidate pairs in one list, replacing InfoNCE and per-query AP losses
AsDkLi7mAk.problem: Per-query losses such as InfoNCE and per-query AP surrogates ignore whether similarities are comparable across queries, which any system with a single decision threshold relies on.
AsDkLi7mAk.method: gSAP is a differentiable surrogate of global Average Precision computed from a similarity matrix and a binary positive-pair matrix, ranking all pairs in the batch jointly; it is a drop-in replacement for existing losses and stays trainable at low temperatures.
AsDkLi7mAk.key_idea: Apply one smooth AP surrogate to the flattened batch similarity matrix instead of per query, so similarities become consistent across queries.
AsDkLi7mAk.evidence: Swapping gSAP into established recipes for supervised metric learning, cross-modal alignment and self-supervised pretraining, evaluated with gAP and shared-threshold F1 (for example on SOP and Met per reviewers).
AsDkLi7mAk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the cross-query consistency issue practically meaningful and the empirical study extensive, with evaluations (gAP, shared-threshold F1) that directly target the claimed benefit.
AsDkLi7mAk.main_concern: Novelty is limited (essentially Smooth-AP applied to the flattened matrix, with an existing gAP metric), baselines such as PNP are missing, and the cost may be cubic in batch size.

Q9UhSURI9U.one_liner: Training-free sparse episodic memory archives selected text and replays retrieved evidence through a linear-attention model's native forward pass
Q9UhSURI9U.problem: Linear attention's fixed-size recurrent state must support ongoing computation and also preserve an ever-growing history, so its memory capacity is presumed to cap long-context capability.
Q9UhSURI9U.method: NoteBank archives selected text before future queries are known, uses the backbone's native features for writing and addressing, and reads retrieved evidence via replay through the native forward computation, with no external embedding model, trained retriever or separate reader.
Q9UhSURI9U.key_idea: Offload long-term storage from the recurrent state to a sparse episodic memory that is written, addressed and read using the backbone's own features and forward pass.
Q9UhSURI9U.evidence: Six RULER retrieval tasks at one million tokens, LongBench v1/v2 and MemoryAgentBench, on three 1.3B recurrent backbones plus post-trained Mamba-2-8B and Qwen3.5-9B.
Q9UhSURI9U.claimed_gains: At one million tokens it raises Gated DeltaNet's mean accuracy across six RULER retrieval tasks from 1.7% to 70.3%, adds at most 0.025% to analytical FLOPs, and uses persistent storage about 1/2600 of a Transformer's full MHA KV cache.
Q9UhSURI9U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the training-free, plug-and-play design simple and practical, with large million-token retrieval gains across recurrent architectures and clear presentation.
Q9UhSURI9U.main_concern: Gains on real-world long-context tasks are limited and some baselines are mismatched (a clean-start baseline already reaches most of the Mamba-2-8B gain, and no RAG comparison), so the RULER-style needle gains may overstate the benefit.

o0eustAJW1.one_liner: Controlled task suite tests few-shot in-context learning across six modalities and checks whether per-task benefits correlate across them.
o0eustAJW1.problem: It is unclear whether few-shot in-context learning emerges broadly beyond language and, if so, what difficulty profile is shared across modalities.
o0eustAJW1.method: Instantiates the same paired-mapping task suite (8-bit transformations per reviews) in language, genome, integer sequences, time series, images and proteins, with label-shuffled controls and per-trial resampled mappings, then compares per-task ICL effects across modalities.
o0eustAJW1.key_idea: Render one paired-mapping task suite in every modality and test whether tasks that benefit from ICL in one modality also benefit in others (Convergent Emergence Hypothesis).
o0eustAJW1.evidence: Paired-mapping ICL is shown in six modalities to exceed controlled baselines, with correlated per-task effects across five of them, supported by mathematical arguments for the control design.
o0eustAJW1.claimed_gains: Paired-mapping ICL emerges across six modalities, surpasses controlled baselines, and has correlated per-task effects across five of them.
o0eustAJW1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the cross-modality evidence for ICL is a useful record, the controlled design (label-shuffled control, resampled mappings) is sound, and limitations are discussed transparently.
o0eustAJW1.main_concern: The task domain is narrow (8-bit bitstring transformations) and divergences such as images are unexplained or confounded by tokenization, so the convergence evidence is weak and gives little insight into why ICL differs across modalities.

vBDoCo83OY.one_liner: Interprets self-conditioning in flow language models as fixed-point iteration and distills it into few-step flow-map language models.
vBDoCo83OY.problem: Self-conditioning improves flow-based language models but its gains are poorly understood, and it is unclear how to use it with few-step flow-map generators.
vBDoCo83OY.method: Shows self-conditioned flow models perform a fixed-point iteration, defines fixed-point flows as a two-dimensional class (flow process by fixed-point iteration) that give valid flow maps, and distills them with fixed-point distillation for the iterations and flow map distillation for the flow process, producing FMLM*.
vBDoCo83OY.key_idea: Self-conditioning is treated as a hidden fixed-point iteration, so compressing both the iteration and the flow process by distillation yields a single flow map for few-step generation.
vBDoCo83OY.evidence: OpenWebText experiments on two self-conditioned flow language model families (ELF and LangFlow) measuring GPT-2 Large perplexity and entropy, covering iterative refinement, warm versus cold starts, and online and offline distillation.
vBDoCo83OY.claimed_gains: FMLM* outperforms prior self-conditioned and few-step models in one- and few-step generation on OpenWebText, with no numbers given in the abstract.
vBDoCo83OY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the fixed-point view is a clear, useful explanation of self-conditioning that motivates a practical distillation method with improved few-step quality.
vBDoCo83OY.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to OpenWebText with small models and mainly gPPL-entropy metrics, and comparisons at different entropy levels do not settle the quality-versus-diversity trade-off.

PZtabdsl7E.one_liner: HVFT fine-tunes a pretrained generator to maximize expected hypervolume via marginal-hypervolume rewards in KL-proximal subproblems.
PZtabdsl7E.problem: Steering pretrained flow and diffusion generators toward complementary multi-objective trade-offs is hard because inference-time search is costly and fixed per-candidate rewards ignore how designs complement one another.
PZtabdsl7E.method: Adapts a single pretrained generator to maximize the expected hypervolume of its samples while limiting departure from the pretrained distribution. The first variation of expected hypervolume equals the expected marginal hypervolume contribution, estimated unbiasedly from model samples, giving an adaptive reward for a sequence of KL-proximal scalar-reward subproblems.
PZtabdsl7E.key_idea: The first variation of expected hypervolume is each candidate's expected marginal hypervolume contribution, giving an adaptive scalar reward that lets KL-proximal fine-tuning optimize a non-per-candidate objective.
PZtabdsl7E.evidence: Proofs of concavity, relative smoothness and convergence, plus experiments on two drug-design tasks (molecules and peptides) with flow and diffusion model families against inference-time guidance and fine-tuning baselines.
PZtabdsl7E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the first-variation identity is clean and the theory rigorous, with consistent hypervolume gains and more retained diversity than several fine-tuning baselines across tasks and model families.
PZtabdsl7E.main_concern: The method builds heavily on Flow Density Control (De Santi et al., 2025), hypervolume is both the training objective and main metric, and comparisons do not fix a computational budget or account for low validity.

k6thgLDk5O.one_liner: Post-training method that fine-tunes a Schrodinger bridge toward a reward-tilted target via alternating optimization and Adjoint Matching.
k6thgLDk5O.problem: Adapting a pretrained Schrodinger bridge to rewards such as human preferences or physical constraints is underexplored, unlike reward tilting for diffusion models.
k6thgLDk5O.method: TSBM fine-tunes a learned bridge between source p0 and target p1 toward a reward-tilted target proportional to p1 times exp(r) while preserving the source p0. It is formulated as alternating optimization initialized from the pretrained bridge, with theoretical justification and a practical algorithm based on Adjoint Matching.
k6thgLDk5O.key_idea: Alternate controller and corrector updates, using Adjoint Matching with the pretrained bridge as reference, to tilt the target marginal by a reward while keeping the source fixed.
k6thgLDk5O.evidence: Unpaired image-to-image translation targeting digit properties in MNIST and facial attributes in CelebA, with theoretical justification.
k6thgLDk5O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mathematical formulation is clear and well grounded, handles the input-output dependence of bridges, and builds reward guidance into model parameters without extra reward evaluations at inference.
k6thgLDk5O.main_concern: Cost and thin validation: fine-tuning needs repeated SDE and adjoint simulations, post-training baselines are missing, and convergence results rely on exact-update and regularity assumptions.

JW6zLHoJTp.one_liner: ReDT maps each view to fixed-size basis tokens, attends in that compact space, and projects back for high-resolution reconstruction.
JW6zLHoJTp.problem: Visual geometry transformers are trained at fixed standard-definition resolutions and degrade and scale poorly at high resolution because within-frame and backbone attention remain expensive.
JW6zLHoJTp.method: ReDT first maps each view to a fixed-size set of basis tokens, computes correspondences in this constant-size basis space, then projects the outputs back to the original resolution for dense prediction.
JW6zLHoJTp.key_idea: Decouple the attention representation from input resolution by computing correspondences among a fixed number of basis tokens per view and projecting results back to pixels.
JW6zLHoJTp.evidence: Experiments on multiple datasets spanning SD to FHD (2K) inputs, including ETH3D at 2K, with scaling and ablation studies.
JW6zLHoJTp.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract text is cut off before the ETH3D (2K) numbers and only claims better reconstruction quality and efficiency than existing visual geometry transformers.
JW6zLHoJTp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree ReDT gives strong accuracy and efficiency gains on high-resolution inputs, backed by extensive evaluation, ablations and a useful analysis of resolution sensitivity.
JW6zLHoJTp.main_concern: Why HD inputs are worth using is not convincingly shown (Chamfer Distance barely improves from 1K to 2K and degrades at 4K), and the DIVA block is hard to follow and of unclear novelty.

e972ELXH6t.one_liner: Shifted Legendre expansions of the Brownian path with a Wong-Zakai objective enable derivative-based training of stochastic flow maps.
e972ELXH6t.problem: Training stochastic flow maps is hard because the Brownian path is infinite-dimensional and nowhere differentiable, which blocks the derivative-based losses used for deterministic flow maps.
e972ELXH6t.method: They represent the Brownian path with a shifted Legendre polynomial basis that carries higher-order local information and train with a Wong-Zakai-style objective that forces the network to use the full path representation. They also give a recipe to fine-tune large pretrained flow models into stochastic flow maps.
e972ELXH6t.key_idea: Smooth the Brownian driver with a shifted Legendre expansion so a Wong-Zakai objective can apply derivative-based flow-map losses using higher-order path information.
e972ELXH6t.evidence: Ablations on toy problems and ImageNet fine-tuning of a large flow model, plus a low-dimensional Feynman-Kac corrector experiment described in the reviews.
e972ELXH6t.claimed_gains: Roughly a three-fold improvement in FD-DINOv2 at four NFE on ImageNet.
e972ELXH6t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the combination of smooth Brownian-path representations and Wong-Zakai objectives a principled, coherent fix that yields substantial few-step generation gains.
e972ELXH6t.main_concern: Evidence is stronger for sample quality than for fidelity to the intended SDE, since pathwise consistency is measured against the model's own 32-step rollout rather than a high-accuracy SDE solution.

cxEfojSkHO.one_liner: Pretraining neural CFD surrogates on pooled steady-state datasets across geometries and fidelities improves zero- and few-shot transfer.
cxEfojSkHO.problem: Neural CFD surrogates generalize poorly beyond their training geometries and applications, and the usual fix of generating a new dataset requires costly numerical solvers.
cxEfojSkHO.method: They study surrogates trained across different geometries, boundary conditions and fidelities, then fine-tune the pretrained cross-domain model on held-out datasets, analyzing model size, dataset diversity, normalization and domain ambiguity.
cxEfojSkHO.key_idea: Simply pool steady-state CFD datasets from different domains for pretraining, which is sufficient and effective regardless of architecture.
cxEfojSkHO.evidence: Three architectures evaluated on four unseen datasets, with zero- and few-shot comparisons against training from scratch and domain-specific experts.
cxEfojSkHO.claimed_gains: Finetuning a pretrained cross-domain model achieves 2-3x lower errors at the same sample size and uses 8x fewer samples to reach the same error, compared with training from scratch.
cxEfojSkHO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that cross-domain pretraining consistently reduces zero- and few-shot error across the tested architectures and is practically valuable for data-limited CFD users.
cxEfojSkHO.main_concern: The method is plain dataset pooling with limited novelty, and the dataset-specific normalization uses target-set ground-truth statistics, which may inflate zero-shot results.

MbwCn5aoIR.one_liner: Cyber-range benchmark of 110 vulnerabilities and eight multi-host ranges testing whether frontier AI agents sustain stateful, multi-stage attacks.
MbwCn5aoIR.problem: Existing benchmarks evaluate bounded tasks around single vulnerabilities, whereas real intrusions are open-ended and stateful, so agents' ability to sustain realistic cyberattacks is poorly understood.
MbwCn5aoIR.method: AgentCyberRange has 110 vulnerabilities across 15 real web applications and eight enterprise-like multi-host cyber ranges with 156 hosts, spanning web exploitation and post-exploitation. State-coupled attack chains require progress to carry across stages, and effect-based oracles with PoC-aware verification judge open-ended attack paths.
MbwCn5aoIR.key_idea: Couple attack stages through state so credentials and footholds carry across hosts, and verify success by effects and PoC checks rather than fixed solution paths.
MbwCn5aoIR.evidence: Seven frontier AI systems evaluated under matched prompts and budgets on web-exploitation and post-exploitation tasks.
MbwCn5aoIR.claimed_gains: The strongest system, GPT-5.6-Sol with Codex, solves 36.1% of web-exploitation tasks and 78.1% of post-exploitation tasks, and agents also discover previously unknown vulnerabilities.
MbwCn5aoIR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the benchmark large, expert-designed and realistic, and see its state-dependent multi-stage evaluation and failure-mode findings as valuable.
MbwCn5aoIR.main_concern: Reviewers question evaluation validity: model and scaffold effects cannot be separated, the post-exploitation metric measures partial compromise with a weaker verifier rather than completed attack chains, and zero-day and leakage claims lack verification.

NFRnhbCokv.one_liner: Estimates transduced-LM prefix probabilities unbiasedly by sampling source prefixes without replacement and reweighting by inverse inclusion probability.
NFRnhbCokv.problem: A target-prefix probability under a transduced language model sums over a possibly infinite set of source strings, and prior work uses a shortcut and biased pruning to make breadth-first search feasible.
NFRnhbCokv.method: The algorithm samples source prefixes without replacement and reweights each by the inverse of its inclusion probability, giving an unbiased estimate that also quantifies the mass lost by pruning. The number of prefixes shrinks as more probability mass is added to the running estimate, which guarantees the run halts with probability one.
NFRnhbCokv.key_idea: Replace biased beam pruning with without-replacement sampling of source prefixes reweighted by inverse inclusion probability, giving an unbiased prefix-probability estimator.
NFRnhbCokv.evidence: Five experimental settings covering subword-to-word conversion on English text, DNA-to-amino-acid transduction, comparison with sequential Monte Carlo baselines and a repeated published reading-time analysis, using GPT-2 models.
NFRnhbCokv.claimed_gains: Better compute-variance tradeoff for subword-to-whole-word conversion on English text, lower error than sequential Monte Carlo baselines on DNA-to-amino-acid transduction, and runtime reduced by orders of magnitude there.
NFRnhbCokv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the unbiased estimator with proofs a reasonable fix for prior pruning bias, one that works in high-entropy settings where pruning fails and allows quantifying variance.
NFRnhbCokv.main_concern: Speedups may be specific to settings like DNA-to-amino-acid transduction, pruning bias has little practical effect on text, and the evaluation uses only GPT-2 models and measures estimation accuracy rather than usefulness of the transduced model.

CIn8XwY0G4.one_liner: Financial foundation model using 256-bit binary candlestick tokens, conditional flow-matching generation, and reward-guided post-training via ReFLO.
CIn8XwY0G4.problem: Scaling generative pretraining on market data makes categorical next-token prediction over high-capacity token spaces expensive, and sequence-modeling objectives are only indirectly aligned with downstream quantitative metrics.
CIn8XwY0G4.method: Each candlestick bar is encoded as a 256-bit binary token (an implicit 2^256 code space) and next-token generation uses conditional flow matching. ReFLO (Rejected-Future Flow Optimization) uses verifiable financial rewards to select low-scoring futures and builds repulsive token-level regression targets, without differentiating through rewards or evaluating policy likelihoods.
CIn8XwY0G4.key_idea: Generate binary market tokens jointly with conditional flow matching, and post-train by regressing away from low-reward sampled futures.
CIn8XwY0G4.evidence: Experiments across quantitative finance tasks, including zero-shot return forecasting, a scaling ladder, and ReFLO post-training; reviews note a fixed test period of roughly half a year.
CIn8XwY0G4.claimed_gains: FiRE improves return forecasting IC by 44% over the strongest baseline in the zero-shot setting, with the gain increasing to 51% after ReFLO post-training.
CIn8XwY0G4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree binary tokenization with flow-based generation is a practical way to scale market representation capacity, the problem is important, and the experiments across financial tasks are extensive.
CIn8XwY0G4.main_concern: Results lack significance tests or multi-seed variance, rely on a short fixed test period, and omit baselines such as LightGBM and XGBoost.

zE8ngOW6Gg.one_liner: Unsupervised aerial-ground person re-ID that clusters both views jointly with dynamic neighbor allocation and reweights noisy pseudo-labels.
zE8ngOW6Gg.problem: Existing unsupervised AG-ReID methods cluster within each view and then match across views, so clustering errors cascade and amplify, leaving pseudo-labels unreliable.
zE8ngOW6Gg.method: Global dynamic clustering (GDC) jointly clusters aerial and ground images while dynamically adjusting the proportion of each view among each image's K nearest neighbors. Label dynamic weighting (LDW) reweights pseudo-labels, and a mixture-pure contrastive loss uses single-view clusters to supplement cross-view supervision.
zE8ngOW6Gg.key_idea: Cluster aerial and ground images together with an adaptive per-view neighbor ratio, then down-weight likely-noisy pseudo-labels in training.
zE8ngOW6Gg.evidence: Experiments on AG-ReID.v1 and LAGPeR with ablations; reviews note GGC is the only same-setting baseline.
zE8ngOW6Gg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pipeline is clear and addresses a concrete failure mode, error cascading in two-stage pseudo-labeling, with encouraging results and complementary components.
zE8ngOW6Gg.main_concern: Comparisons are thin, with GGC as the only same-setting baseline and inconsistent evaluation protocols, and the dynamic neighbor allocation in GDC lacks justification that it differs from a fixed ratio.

AsfMBPQMiJ.one_liner: Ab initio cryo-EM reconstruction that jointly optimizes particle poses and anisotropic Gaussians using frequency marching and adaptive densification.
AsfMBPQMiJ.problem: Most Gaussian-based cryo-EM methods assume known particle poses, while ab initio reconstruction must jointly estimate density and poses, which is severely ill-posed.
AsfMBPQMiJ.method: cryoSplat2 jointly optimizes poses and anisotropic Gaussian representations from random initialization, combining frequency marching for coarse-to-fine pose and structure refinement, adaptive Gaussian densification, and an optimized differentiable splatting operator for efficient pose inference.
AsfMBPQMiJ.key_idea: Coordinate coarse-to-fine frequency marching with progressively densified Gaussians to jointly refine poses and density from random initialization.
AsfMBPQMiJ.evidence: Multiple real cryo-EM datasets compared with cryoSPARC and cryoDRGN-AI (reviews mention EMPIAR-10028).
AsfMBPQMiJ.claimed_gains: Robustly reconstructs 3D structures on real datasets without an initial reference or given poses, including challenging cases involving cryoSPARC or cryoDRGN-AI; the abstract is cut off and gives no numbers.
AsfMBPQMiJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well written and the real-data experiments are convincing, showing Gaussian-based ab initio reconstruction works and is much faster than cryoDRGN-AI.
AsfMBPQMiJ.main_concern: Technical novelty is modest because densification and the scheduler adapt existing techniques, components are not ablated separately, and robustness is not quantified with run counts and success rates.

KcSYdf3gss.one_liner: Ground-truth-free on-policy self-distillation that teaches OmniLLMs to reason over compressed audio-video tokens from a full-context teacher.
KcSYdf3gss.problem: Aggressive audio-video token compression lowers OmniLLM accuracy, and adapting the language model to reason over the remaining compressed context is under-explored.
KcSYdf3gss.method: CAFD adapts an OmniLLM to a fixed compression pipeline by using the full-token view of the same sample as privileged information: a full-context teacher guides a compressed-context student, with no reference answers, rationales, or correctness rewards.
KcSYdf3gss.key_idea: Distill on-policy from the model's own full-token view into its compressed-context view, requiring no labels.
KcSYdf3gss.evidence: Qwen2.5-Omni-7B across five audio-video benchmarks, five compression pipelines, and five deployment budgets.
KcSYdf3gss.claimed_gains: Improves 120 out of 125 conditions with an average accuracy boost of 1.44 points and recovers 26.9% of the accuracy gap on average.
KcSYdf3gss.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method practical because it needs no labels or task-specific prompts, with gains that are consistent across five compression pipelines and reusable from a single checkpoint.
KcSYdf3gss.main_concern: Reviewers say the paper does not isolate the contribution of its on-policy, EMA-teacher design versus simpler baselines such as supervised fine-tuning on teacher outputs, and overlaps heavily with existing on-policy self-distillation work.

ubOeoowY6F.one_liner: Contextual-bandit routing among robot policy, VLM planner, and human help using one Bayesian belief with Thompson sampling.
ubOeoowY6F.problem: Routing controllers trained on atomic tasks face compositional multi-step instructions out of distribution, and need distance-aware uncertainty and cost-aware exploration to choose among execution modes.
ubOeoowY6F.method: BARM casts assistance routing as a contextual bandit with heterogeneous arm costs; a single Bayesian belief state whose epistemic variance grows with distance from training data drives reward modeling, Thompson Sampling exploration, and online adaptation. A sublinear Bayesian regret bound is shown under the well-specified linear-reward regime.
ubOeoowY6F.key_idea: One Bayesian belief with distance-aware epistemic variance feeds Thompson Sampling over net rewards, so unseen tasks look uncertain and trigger cost-aware assistance.
ubOeoowY6F.evidence: CALVIN, LIBERO, and other settings (abstract truncated), all in simulation per reviewers, plus a regret bound for the linear-reward regime.
ubOeoowY6F.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the contextual-bandit formulation of executor selection sound and well motivated, with a lightweight method and evaluation across a wide range of setups and baselines.
ubOeoowY6F.main_concern: Reviewers question the fairness and completeness of the comparison, since the human-assistance arm inflates success and a hierarchical VLM-plus-diffusion-policy baseline is missing, and note experiments are simulation-only.

zJtGycZulV.one_liner: UltraMatch routes only a few candidate target blocks per source block, restricting token-level matching to avoid the dense matching matrix.
zJtGycZulV.problem: Coarse matching in semi-dense matchers builds dense token-to-token matrices whose quadratic computation and memory cost limits speed and resolution.
zJtGycZulV.method: A lightweight Transport Path Router ranks candidate target blocks for each source block from coarse block representations and keeps a small set; a sparse global Dual-Softmax matches only within routed candidates while retaining global competition, and structural reparameterization with a tiny shared fine matching head cuts cost further.
zJtGycZulV.key_idea: Route each source block to a few target blocks using coarse block representations, then run Dual-Softmax only over routed candidates with global competition retained.
zJtGycZulV.evidence: Comparisons with semi-dense matchers and SuperPoint+LightGlue; reviews cite MegaDepth AUC@5, ablations of routing and sparse global normalization, and routing added to ELoFTR, JamMA and EDM.
zJtGycZulV.claimed_gains: Competitive accuracy among semi-dense matchers while running 1.67x faster than SuperPoint+LightGlue with only 0.44 GiB peak inference memory, enabling inference up to 6K resolution on a single RTX 3090.
zJtGycZulV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the accuracy-efficiency trade-off attractive, with routing applicable to several matcher architectures (ELoFTR, JamMA, EDM) and the sparse global normalization supported by ablation.
zJtGycZulV.main_concern: Comparison with simpler candidate-reduction alternatives (feature filtering such as SLiM, pooled-feature block selection, coarse-to-fine search) is insufficient, and conceptual novelty beyond EDM plus a routing stage is limited.

3GDTfB50ms.one_liner: Turns AND-OR retrosynthesis search structure into local turn-level advantages with provenance tracing for agentic RL, without a critic.
3GDTfB50ms.problem: Trajectory-level rewards for LLM retrosynthesis agents do not distinguish how individual search decisions contribute, since equally rewarded trajectories may resolve different precursor subgoals.
3GDTfB50ms.method: PTPO aggregates terminal precursor assessments over the AND-OR synthesis structure, computes local advantages by comparing decisions for the same molecule under identical ordered candidate views, and propagates them by provenance tracing to the earlier turns that revealed the selected candidates. Separate turn-level and trajectory-level PPO objectives use independently normalized advantages and reuse the sampled trajectories.
3GDTfB50ms.key_idea: Score each reaction choice by downstream precursor completion in the AND-OR tree, and credit the earlier query turns that surfaced the chosen candidate.
3GDTfB50ms.evidence: Experiments with a 4B agent trained with PTPO (details truncated), with Pass@1 at different search budgets and ablations per the reviews.
3GDTfB50ms.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the local supervision fits the task structure, extracts information that terminal rewards miss without extra rollouts or a critic, and gives substantial gains over the non-fine-tuned agent.
3GDTfB50ms.main_concern: Reaction scores may not reflect decision quality because they confound downstream search and rely on heuristics such as a fixed 0.5 value for open branches, and novelty over GiGPO is unclear since it is not a baseline.

yLeGwz8GDb.one_liner: Scores analogy quality with a category-theoretic pullback over VLM-extracted relation graphs and uses it as feedback to refine generated images.
yLeGwz8GDb.problem: AI multimodal analogy generation lacks an interpretable measure of whether relational structure is understood and preserved in the generated output.
yLeGwz8GDb.method: PRISM represents analogies as explicit relational mappings grounded in category theory, with VLMs instantiating the structures across modalities, and its pullback score quantifies relational alignment from the resulting graph. An iterative loop uses the score as in-context feedback to revise the generated image toward greater relational depth.
yLeGwz8GDb.key_idea: Compute a pullback score over cross-domain relation mappings extracted by VLMs, and feed it back in context to iteratively revise the image.
yLeGwz8GDb.evidence: AnaloBench for the pullback score, and VLM-as-a-judge and human evaluations of visual metaphor generation.
yLeGwz8GDb.claimed_gains: Selecting the correct analogy by pullback score alone reaches 82.5% accuracy on AnaloBench, and human participants prefer the refined output in 57.65% of pairwise comparisons.
yLeGwz8GDb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the explicit, inspectable relational representation is more interpretable than black-box judgments, with convincing qualitative examples and empirical results.
yLeGwz8GDb.main_concern: The score's validity and the refinement gains are not isolated: it can reward shortcuts such as crowded images and text labels, the refinement feedback includes more than the score, and a reviewer could not reproduce the ablation table from the provided code.

7sCSuITONr.one_liner: Training-free inference-time framework that reattributes host-object scores and rectifies part score maps for fine-grained referring segmentation.
7sCSuITONr.problem: VLM-based segmentation assigns referential focus to the host-object instead of the target part, and the resulting part score map can be incomplete or drift into irrelevant regions.
7sCSuITONr.method: Referential Attribution Reformulation turns the host-object into guidance for target-part localization, and Bidirectional Collaborative Rectification refines the initial part score map by recovering missing regions and suppressing drift-prone activations using internal target-part support and structural affinity. No fine-grained annotations or parameter updates are used.
7sCSuITONr.key_idea: Use the host-object score map as a visual scope for the part query, then refine the part score map with bidirectional support and structural-affinity rectification at inference.
7sCSuITONr.evidence: Experiments across different vision-language segmentation paradigms; a reviewer cites RefCOCOm val-Part mIoU rising from 21.3 to 24.4 for LISA-7B, 24.5 to 27.4 for M2SA, and 33.4 to 39.8 for Qwen3-VL plus SAM.
7sCSuITONr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the host-versus-part confusion is a meaningful failure mode and the training-free, host-guided approach is intuitive, clearly illustrated, and improves several base models.
7sCSuITONr.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty over host-to-part propagation work such as HOPS, reliance on the base model's host-object score map without robustness analysis, and inconsistent table numbers (23.1 vs 22.1).

Rsl5OMHAGB.one_liner: Sparse-autoencoder latent directions and weight orthogonalization separate task intent from safety signals to produce jailbreaks without per-prompt optimization.
Rsl5OMHAGB.problem: Attack success alone does not reveal whether compliance comes from preserved task intent, suppressed safety signals, or attack-specific artifacts.
Rsl5OMHAGB.method: CFA^2 is a white-box framework that uses Pearl's front-door adjustment to motivate separating task-relevant semantics from safety-related variation in LLM latent space, using Sparse Autoencoders, contrastive datasets, and weight orthogonalization. After offline calibration it generates attacks without per-prompt iterative optimization.
Rsl5OMHAGB.key_idea: Pair jailbroken variants of prompts to fix task semantics while varying safety behavior, identify safety directions with sparse autoencoders, and orthogonalize weights against them.
Rsl5OMHAGB.evidence: Evaluated on HarmBench across four open-source LLMs, with same-family black-box prompt transfer; reviewers note a contrastive dataset calibrated from HarmBench and AdvBench and generation within two seconds.
Rsl5OMHAGB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the task-matched contrast and SAE-based direction identification and note the method is fast, clear, and effective on HarmBench.
Rsl5OMHAGB.main_concern: Baselines and LLM versions are dated, only HarmBench is used, steering and latent-adversarial-training baselines are missing, and the assumption of content invariance between paired prompts is not justified.

cImYuw3mTU.one_liner: SAM3RL replaces SAM 3's memory update rules with a lightweight RL-trained controller choosing which frames enter the memory bank
cImYuw3mTU.problem: The SAM 3 tracker manages its memory bank with a simple first-in-first-out rule, and hand-crafted memory rules developed for SAM 2 transfer only partially to the stronger SAM 3 backbone.
cImYuw3mTU.method: Extends the SAM 3 tracker with a lightweight memory controller trained by reinforcement learning that decides which frames enter the memory bank to maximize tracking performance, with the backbone frozen. The same approach applied to SAM 2 gives SAM2RL.
cImYuw3mTU.key_idea: Cast memory-bank eviction as a sequential decision problem and train a small policy by reinforcement learning, with the backbone frozen, to choose which frames to keep.
cImYuw3mTU.evidence: 12 tracking and video object segmentation benchmarks, comparing SAM3RL and SAM2RL with hand-crafted memory rules.
cImYuw3mTU.claimed_gains: SAM3RL sets a new state of the art on 10 of the 12 tracking and video object segmentation benchmarks, outperforming all hand-crafted rules without runtime overhead, and SAM2RL outperforms hand-crafted rules on 9 of the 12 benchmarks.
cImYuw3mTU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear MDP formulation of memory control with a frozen backbone and the evidence that the learned controller generalizes beyond training videos and also improves segmentation.
cImYuw3mTU.main_concern: The gain from learned eviction is not isolated from other system components, and comparisons rely on unofficial SAM 3 ports of hand-crafted rules that keep their SAM 2 hyperparameters.

nqnPeRtbh0.one_liner: Face-clustering attention that replaces hard Top-K masks with entmax sparse attention and adds graph-structured encodings and adjacency-guided biases.
nqnPeRtbh0.problem: KNN graphs for large-scale face clustering contain false-positive and false-negative edges, and the strongest denoiser, Diff-Cluster, uses non-differentiable hard Top-K masks and sequence-centric positional encodings.
nqnPeRtbh0.method: DASA replaces hard Top-K with entmax sparse distributions under a learnable per-head temperature, consolidating multi-branch MoE routing into one branch. GSDA injects degree and multi-hop random-walk encodings into queries and keys and applies opposite adjacency-guided biases to the two differential attention maps.
nqnPeRtbh0.key_idea: Use entmax with learnable temperature for differentiable sparse support, and bias the two differential attention maps oppositely by graph adjacency.
nqnPeRtbh0.evidence: Per the reviews, experiments on MS1M at five scales against Diff-Cluster, reporting Pairwise and BCubed F-scores plus parameters, FLOPs, and latency; the abstract's results are cut off.
nqnPeRtbh0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree each design choice targets a specific Diff-Cluster limitation, the method is clearly written, and it improves accuracy while cutting parameters, FLOPs, and latency.
nqnPeRtbh0.main_concern: Conceptual novelty is limited since entmax sparse attention and graph-informed attention biases are established, and the graph-bias mechanism is under-validated against corrupted graphs.

b4gksCfdgH.one_liner: Post-trains world-action models with action-preserving visual interventions and contrastive state correspondence for robustness to appearance changes.
b4gksCfdgH.problem: World-action models retain appearance details for video prediction, but robust control needs invariance to task-irrelevant appearance changes, and action supervision does not identify which visually different observations share the same manipulation state.
b4gksCfdgH.method: CausalWAM varies scene appearance while preserving robot-object geometry, task instructions, and demonstrated actions. A contrastive objective aligns alternative renderings of the same state and separates different states, and a shared content reader supplies compact tokens to the action expert alongside its native visual conditioning.
b4gksCfdgH.key_idea: Render the same manipulation state under different appearances and contrast those renderings against other states, routing the result to the action expert through a shared content reader.
b4gksCfdgH.evidence: RoboTwin 2.0 Randomized with action demonstrations restricted to Clean scenes, seven unseen LIBERO-Plus perturbation types, and real-robot experiments under visual disturbance.
b4gksCfdgH.claimed_gains: CausalWAM-Joint raises RoboTwin 2.0 Randomized success from 1.9% for FastWAM to 34.7%, reaches 79.4% mean success across seven unseen LIBERO-Plus perturbation types, and improves real-robot success under visual disturbance from 13.3% (end value truncated in the abstract).
b4gksCfdgH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the learning signal is well motivated for visual robustness and that paired renderings with a contrastive loss give substantial robustness gains on LIBERO-Plus and real robots.
b4gksCfdgH.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate the contrastive loss in CausalWAM-Joint, and missing matched baselines trained on the same randomized images leave unclear how much of the gain comes from contrastive learning versus more varied data or added modules.

UPSjUUMsZF.one_liner: Makes observation models and experimental controls editable in a typed theory representation to expose when law rewrites absorb instrument defects.
UPSjUUMsZF.problem: Law-discovery systems hold observation models and controls fixed, so a perfect fit can assign an instrument defect to the wrong physical mechanism without the system noticing.
UPSjUUMsZF.method: Theories are typed structures whose observation models, admissible values, and controls can be edited, and repairs are generated from this structure. For linear systems they derive a dimensional criterion predicting when an exact law-only explanation exists, and for each repair the system reports whether data, edit cost, or neither decides and proposes a discriminating measurement.
UPSjUUMsZF.key_idea: Treat the measurement model and controls as repairable theory components, detect absorption where a rewritten law reproduces an instrument defect exactly, and propose measurements that separate explanations.
UPSjUUMsZF.evidence: A mass-spring apparatus with a lagging sensor, 100 systems of each kind, and the DiscoverPhysics benchmark where frontier-model agents face two worlds with identical recordings.
UPSjUUMsZF.claimed_gains: Two law edits reproduce the lagging-sensor recording to 5.1e-16 relative error, and across 100 systems of each kind the system reports that only the cost separates the explanations and the added measurement identifies the true mechanism.
UPSjUUMsZF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the thesis that a perfect fit can misattribute an instrument defect is important and clearly presented, with the mass-spring example as a useful anchor.
UPSjUUMsZF.main_concern: Novelty is limited because absorption and identifiability are well known in classical system identification and control, and edit cost as the repair selector is weakly justified.

fhJE446OXg.one_liner: Proves nearly matching ReLU approximation bounds for smooth Hilbert-space functionals under joint decay of coordinate magnitudes and directional sensitivities.
fhJE446OXg.problem: Approximation theory for deep learning on functional data does not capture the varying importance of coordinates in a basis expansion of an infinite-dimensional input.
fhJE446OXg.method: Represents the functional input in a basis and combines coordinate truncation, anisotropic partitioning, local Taylor approximation and ReLU network realization, allowing unrestricted interactions among retained coordinates. It proves a nonasymptotic uniform upper bound and a pseudo-dimension-based lower bound.
fhJE446OXg.key_idea: Measure each coordinate's importance by basis-score magnitude and directional sensitivity, and truncate to a budget-dependent effective dimension before Taylor-approximating with ReLU networks.
fhJE446OXg.evidence: Theoretical proofs of a nonasymptotic upper bound and a pseudo-dimension lower bound; no experiments stated.
fhJE446OXg.claimed_gains: Under generalized exponential decay the upper and lower bounds match at leading order, which is stretched-exponential in the logarithm of the network size budget; no numbers stated.
fhJE446OXg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the topic relevant and the budget-dependent effective-dimension formulation intuitive and interpretable.
fhJE446OXg.main_concern: Correctness and novelty are questioned: one reviewer gives a counterexample to Theorem 1 as stated, and another sees limited novelty relative to prior functional-approximation work.

pr9gnbb2bs.one_liner: Proves nearly matching upper and lower bounds on excess population risk of (epsilon, delta)-unlearning for smooth strongly convex losses.
pr9gnbb2bs.problem: The fundamental statistical cost of unlearning in smooth strongly convex stochastic optimization was unclear.
pr9gnbb2bs.method: Proves upper and lower bounds on the excess population risk of approximate unlearning that are tight up to a condition-number factor, and exactly matching for mean estimation over the unit ball. The algorithm achieves pure epsilon-unlearning.
pr9gnbb2bs.key_idea: A pure epsilon-unlearning algorithm whose unlearning penalty interpolates between the retraining rate and an exponentially smaller term as epsilon/d grows, paired with a lower bound for general unlearners.
pr9gnbb2bs.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower bounds, with mean estimation over the unit ball as the case where they match up to constants.
pr9gnbb2bs.claimed_gains: Bounds tight up to a condition-number factor; retraining from scratch is statistically optimal when epsilon is at most of order d, and (epsilon, delta)-unlearning has no statistical advantage over pure epsilon-unlearning.
pr9gnbb2bs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the upper and lower bounds are strong and the techniques elegant, with a lower bound that covers general unlearners.
pr9gnbb2bs.main_concern: Assumptions are restrictive (strong convexity, smoothness, stationary population minimizer), a condition-number gap remains, and the lower-bound idea resembles Sekhari et al. (2021) without credit.

Om69taTbSQ.one_liner: MIRAGE selects edges to reconstruct by maximizing mutual information, enabling graph domain adaptation under missing edges.
Om69taTbSQ.problem: Graph domain adaptation methods assume fully observed topology, but real graphs can have missing edges in source and target, which removes neighborhood information and widens the domain gap.
Om69taTbSQ.method: The paper formulates Edge-Incomplete Graph Domain Adaptation and proposes MIRAGE, which uses mutual information maximization to guide transfer-aware edge selection so that graph reconstruction keeps local information while supporting cross-domain adaptation.
Om69taTbSQ.key_idea: Choose which edges to add during graph reconstruction by maximizing mutual information, so reconstruction is aligned with source-target transfer.
Om69taTbSQ.evidence: Multiple benchmark datasets (four per a review) at several missing-edge ratios, with BFS-based deletion, additional transfer directions and ablations.
Om69taTbSQ.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms competitive baselines under structurally incomplete EIGDA settings; no numbers stated.
Om69taTbSQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is useful and clearly motivated, and that experiments across deletion rates, BFS deletion and ablations show the benefit of combining reconstruction with domain adaptation.
Om69taTbSQ.main_concern: The new setting's distinction from existing structure-learning GDA work is not established, and gains are not isolated to alignment-aware edge reconstruction, for example no report of which edges are added.

LYiP0hfueQ.one_liner: A monitor questions an LLM agent mid-execution to reduce side-objective misbehavior without taking control, evaluated end to end.
LYiP0hfueQ.problem: Passive monitoring may detect harm only after it occurs, while hard intervention prevents harm but disrupts legitimate work.
LYiP0hfueQ.method: Interactive monitoring lets a monitor question an agent during execution so its questions can change the agent's later actions. They evaluate prospectively, measuring side-objective completion, legitimate task performance, intervention burden and what the trajectory reveals about the agent's objectives.
LYiP0hfueQ.key_idea: Let the monitor ask behavior-grounded questions during execution, so communication alone changes the agent's subsequent actions without hard intervention.
LYiP0hfueQ.evidence: SHADE-Arena and ControlArena Django, with expectation-matched control conditions and rollout replicates.
LYiP0hfueQ.claimed_gains: In SHADE-Arena, side-objective completion falls from 46.0% when agents anticipate live oversight to 20.7% when behavior-grounded questions are delivered under the interactive monitor.
LYiP0hfueQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is important, that questioning is a well-posed middle ground between passive monitoring and hard intervention, and that the expectation-matched control design and the observed effect are convincing.
LYiP0hfueQ.main_concern: The utility-preservation claim is thin (wide intervals, adversarial episodes only), prior work reporting the opposite effect (Kusatov et al. 2025a) is not addressed, and prompt-induced adversaries limit conclusions about agents trained to evade monitoring.

OcVNcBSYvo.one_liner: Trains world models on minutes-long spans while each scored chunk attends only to a bounded bank of retrieved co-visible latents.
OcVNcBSYvo.problem: Supervising consistent rendering across revisits needs training samples that span minutes, but dense attention over the full span has quadratic cost.
OcVNcBSYvo.method: A training sample covers a span of any length but is scored only on its last k chunks. Each scored chunk retrieves its own top-K latents by camera co-visibility instead of tokenizing the history, and the union forms a shared bank bounded by kK; at the shortest span the recipe equals conventional training.
OcVNcBSYvo.key_idea: Decouple supervision span from attention: score only the last k chunks, each retrieving top-K latents by camera co-visibility into a shared bank bounded by kK.
OcVNcBSYvo.evidence: Comparison with a sliding-window baseline on revisit consistency across splits, a training-span study from 100 to 400 s, and a bank-swap control that fills the bank from another episode.
OcVNcBSYvo.claimed_gains: Going from 100 to 400 s adds 12% to step time; retrieval raises revisit consistency on every split over a sliding-window baseline, a span reaching the first visit adds a further 24% to 30% at some cost in image quality, and filling the bank from another episode lowers revisit correlation by 83%.
OcVNcBSYvo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it offers a simple, bounded-cost way to separate supervision span from attention context, with solid ablations showing that retrieval and longer spans improve revisit consistency.
OcVNcBSYvo.main_concern: Novelty over Context-as-Memory and WorldMem is not clearly established, and longer spans improve revisit consistency at a cost in image quality, with evaluation mostly on rendered scenes.

CSKf1yaCpE.one_liner: Proves a Diffusion Transformer pretrained across tasks learns the posterior-predictive distribution from demonstrations at a minimax-optimal prompt-length rate.
CSKf1yaCpE.problem: A few demonstrations may fit several tasks, so an in-context generator must sample from a distribution reflecting task uncertainty, and there was no theory of how a DiT learns this.
CSKf1yaCpE.method: The paper identifies the posterior predictive distribution as the generation target and proves a DiT can learn it by score estimation from finitely many pretraining episodes without task labels, with attention aggregating demonstrations and diffusion generating samples.
CSKf1yaCpE.key_idea: Attention aggregates demonstrations into a task posterior while denoising score estimation yields posterior-predictive samples, with error split into learning error and residual task uncertainty.
CSKf1yaCpE.evidence: Theoretical finite-sample guarantees over a Holder class of test-time tasks, plus a small experiment with a conventional DiT showing bimodality and contraction with more demonstrations (per reviews).
CSKf1yaCpE.claimed_gains: The learned DiT attains the minimax-optimal rate in prompt length over a Holder class of test-time tasks with finite-sample guarantees; no numerical values are given.
CSKf1yaCpE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that casting in-context generation as posterior-predictive sampling is clear and that the theoretical analysis, from model capacity to learning from episodes, is strong.
CSKf1yaCpE.main_concern: The analyzed architecture and assumptions (Holder densities with lower bounds, fixed latent task dimension, hand-built tokens) are restrictive and far from practical DiTs, and parts overlap with prior transformer posterior-inference theory.

og6XWSPqRh.one_liner: Tokenizes meshes as per-voxel surface pivots with orientation signs, finer in complex regions, then compresses blocks with a pyramid VAE.
og6XWSPqRh.problem: Irregular mesh topology makes tokenization a geometric sampling problem: how to turn geometric evidence into compact, structured, learnable tokens that still support reconstruction.
og6XWSPqRh.method: Pivot Voxelization represents each active voxel with a surface pivot and orientation sign under a local planarity assumption. Pyramid Pivot Voxelization allocates finer pivot tokens to geometrically complex regions, and a Pyramid VAE learns multi-resolution latent codes over locally reconstructable pivot blocks.
og6XWSPqRh.key_idea: Represent each active voxel by one surface pivot plus an orientation sign that determines corner values for deterministic reconstruction, and allocate pivots adaptively by surface complexity.
og6XWSPqRh.evidence: Reconstruction on ABO, Objaverse and Wild with Chamfer distance, EMD and F-score, plus VAE experiments, as cited in the reviews (abstract truncated).
og6XWSPqRh.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results).
og6XWSPqRh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pivot-and-sign representation is compact with a clear geometric interpretation and gives a favorable reconstruction versus primitive-count trade-off across datasets.
og6XWSPqRh.main_concern: Efficiency is measured only in primitive counts, not full storage cost (spatial coordinates, sampling map, latent sizes), and there is no matched-budget comparison.

hDyYpqWzvA.one_liner: Optimizes input commands of a frozen humanoid behavior foundation model by sampling-based search through closed-loop simulation.
hDyYpqWzvA.problem: Existing humanoid behavior foundation models have a command-execution gap in which executed motions deviate from desired ones, limiting the whole-body accuracy loco-manipulation needs.
hDyYpqWzvA.method: Test-Time Command Optimization (TTCO) adapts the input command to a specific BFM by sampling-based optimization through closed-loop simulations of the BFM and robot dynamics. The authors also derive an approximate compute-optimal scaling strategy and use TTCO to generate BFM-specific action labels from recorded robot trajectories.
hDyYpqWzvA.key_idea: Treat the command as the optimization variable and search over commands with closed-loop BFM-plus-dynamics rollouts until the executed trajectory matches the desired motion, with no retraining.
hDyYpqWzvA.evidence: Three BFMs on the AMASS dataset in simulation, a test-time compute scaling analysis, and simulation and real-robot experiments training loco-manipulation policies from generated labels.
hDyYpqWzvA.claimed_gains: TTCO reduces mean global body-position error by 79-84% in simulation across three BFMs on AMASS.
hDyYpqWzvA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the command-execution gap is a practical problem and that optimizing commands at test time without retraining gives large, consistent tracking gains across BFMs.
hDyYpqWzvA.main_concern: Lower tracking error does not consistently improve downstream policies (SONIC-to-SONIC success falls from 75.8% to 56.7% with optimized labels), and novelty over existing sampling-based control is unclear.

4SNnvv6LxP.one_liner: Embeds cascaded-decomposition components on the Poincare ball by frequency and forecasts via geodesic velocity dynamics, autoregressive or parallel.
4SNnvv6LxP.problem: Euclidean forecasters model multiscale structure without representing the ordering among trend, seasonal and high-frequency components that cascaded decomposition induces.
4SNnvv6LxP.method: HyperForecast embeds decomposed temporal segments on the Poincare ball, with low-frequency components near the origin and high-frequency components near the boundary. It models geodesic velocity either by autoregressive Poincare residual dynamics or by non-autoregressive parallel prediction of all future segments.
4SNnvv6LxP.key_idea: Map the frequency hierarchy of cascaded decomposition onto hyperbolic radial distance and forecast by estimating geodesic velocity on the manifold.
4SNnvv6LxP.evidence: Eleven long-term forecasting benchmarks, with further analysis (abstract truncated).
4SNnvv6LxP.claimed_gains: Outperforms baselines on 9 of 11 long-term forecasting benchmarks, with up to 58% lower mean squared error at long horizons.
4SNnvv6LxP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that linking multiscale decomposition to hyperbolic manifold dynamics is a distinctive geometric perspective with promising results and autoregressive and non-autoregressive variants.
4SNnvv6LxP.main_concern: The frequency ordering is not shown to imply a tree-like hierarchy that warrants hyperbolic geometry (the radial constraint reduces to ranking scaled Euclidean norms), so the motivation is weakly justified.

xxeuDaxOaS.one_liner: Damage-guided local evidence reading for incomplete multimodal sentiment analysis via paired regional erasures.
xxeuDaxOaS.problem: Existing incomplete multimodal sentiment methods rely on global representations and overlook that losing different local regions degrades prediction unevenly, sometimes flipping sentiment polarity.
xxeuDaxOaS.method: DREAM contrasts prediction risks from paired regional erasures to quantify the task relevance of multi-scale local evidence while keeping global summary information. A summary-referenced reader module lets each modality balance a source modality's global summary with its local evidence, conditioned on the receiving modality's available content.
xxeuDaxOaS.key_idea: Estimate the importance of multi-scale local regions from the prediction-risk difference between paired equal-budget erasures, then read that evidence cross-modally conditioned on the receiver's content.
xxeuDaxOaS.evidence: Evaluated on MOSI, MOSEI and CH-SIMS for sentiment classification and regression, without full-view teachers or supervision from fully observed counterparts.
xxeuDaxOaS.claimed_gains: Consistent gains in classification and regression, especially large on CH-SIMS; the exact accuracy and F1 numbers are cut off in the truncated abstract.
xxeuDaxOaS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation of weighting local evidence by task value intuitive and the self-supervised paired-erasure damage signal a reasonable design that needs no complete-view teachers.
xxeuDaxOaS.main_concern: Novelty is questioned as a combination of known local attention, multiscale and cross-modal ideas, with uneven gains across datasets (small on MOSEI) and limited testing under realistic missing patterns.

sYRI7LJlet.one_liner: Hybrid Gaussian ray tracing plus a lightweight neural renderer for relightable, editable real-scene reconstructions.
sYRI7LJlet.problem: Physics-based rendering of Gaussian scenes gives unrealistic relighting because of imperfect geometry, material and light-transport estimates, while pure neural renderers lack an explicit scene for fine-grained editing.
sYRI7LJlet.method: TRON regularizes Gaussian-field materials with intrinsic decomposition priors from a learned inverse rendering model and uses a ray tracer to produce radiometric guidance rather than final pixels. A lightweight single-step neural renderer, trained with a multi-stage strategy, turns these PBR and ray-traced irradiance buffers into photorealistic images.
sYRI7LJlet.key_idea: Treat ray-traced irradiance and PBR buffers from an editable Gaussian field as a 3D scaffold that conditions a lightweight neural renderer to bridge the shading-model-to-photorealism domain gap.
sYRI7LJlet.evidence: Qualitative comparisons against Gaussian baselines and the ray-traced input, quantitative photorealism tables scored by a single VLM evaluator, and ablations of training stages and rendering inputs.
sYRI7LJlet.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract and TLDR claim near-interactive relighting, material editing and object motion but give no numbers.
sYRI7LJlet.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value combining Gaussian ray tracing with neural rendering, the direct editability of captured scenes, clear improvements in shadows, and informative ablations.
sYRI7LJlet.main_concern: The necessity of neural rendering over existing physically based interactive methods is not established, and quantitative photorealism rests on a single VLM evaluator without a user study.

slbhlr9SEs.one_liner: Online RL for LLM agents adding hindsight numerical and language feedback plus UCB-based lesson retrieval.
slbhlr9SEs.problem: Standard RL for LLM agents optimizes only extrinsic task rewards, causing premature convergence to suboptimal policies and leaving experience implicitly encoded in parameters where it is hard to retrieve and reuse.
slbhlr9SEs.method: RetroAgent augments extrinsic rewards with hindsight-generated Intrinsic Numerical Feedback (incremental subtask progress relative to prior attempts) and Intrinsic Language Feedback (textual lessons distilled from successes and failures). Lessons are retrieved with SimUtil-UCB, which balances semantic relevance, historical utility and exploration.
slbhlr9SEs.key_idea: Reward incremental subtask progress against prior attempts and store distilled language lessons, retrieving them with a UCB score that mixes similarity, past utility and exploration.
slbhlr9SEs.evidence: Four agentic benchmarks (ALFWorld, WebShop, Sokoban, MineSweeper) with two model families, compared against GRPO, plus analyses of reward construction, retrieval and reflection mechanisms.
slbhlr9SEs.claimed_gains: Outperforms GRPO by +18.3% on ALFWorld, +15.4% on WebShop, +27.1% on Sokoban, and +8.9% on MineSweeper.
slbhlr9SEs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a coherent framework linking retrospective evaluation, policy optimization and explicit experience retrieval, with broad evaluation across four environments and two model families.
slbhlr9SEs.main_concern: The framework looks mainly compositional: ablations suggest much of the gain over GRPO comes from changed return estimation or numerical feedback alone, and overlap with prior language-feedback work such as Critique-GRPO is not addressed.

OrJmmo9dXI.one_liner: Synthesizes data-analysis tasks by evolving executable workspaces with verified findings, yielding a 5K-trajectory training set.
OrJmmo9dXI.problem: Generating analytics training tasks directly from raw data misses deeper questions that emerge during analysis and gives little evidence for verifying answers.
OrJmmo9dXI.method: DataPraxis progressively enriches workspaces with validated findings and artifacts, then inherits and combines workspaces to uncover deeper questions. Tasks are built from accumulated findings and their dependencies, verified during evolution and after assembly, and the resulting DataPraxis-5K trains DataPraxis-27B and DataPraxis-35B-A3B.
OrJmmo9dXI.key_idea: Accumulate verified findings in executable workspaces, merge workspaces to surface deeper questions, and assemble tasks from the findings' dependencies with verification at each stage.
OrJmmo9dXI.evidence: Training on DataPraxis-5K (5,000 verified trajectories) with dense and MoE backbones, evaluated on three benchmarks including DABStep and JobBench against frontier models and the DataMind synthesis baseline, with ablations on data volume, evolution depth, verification and teacher choice.
OrJmmo9dXI.claimed_gains: DataPraxis-27B achieves 55.11 on DABStep and 51.9 on JobBench, matching or surpassing frontier models such as GLM-5.2.
OrJmmo9dXI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and the downstream gains over the base model substantial across both backbones, with ablations that examine data volume, evolution depth, verification and teacher choice.
OrJmmo9dXI.main_concern: Claims outrun the evidence: DataMind is the only synthesis baseline, only three benchmarks are used, and Table 2 shows the model does not lead any benchmark despite the stated leading performance.

d6WB03h2qI.one_liner: Unsupervised budgeted acquisition of missing sample-view entries for multi-view clustering via conditional information gain.
d6WB03h2qI.problem: Incomplete multi-view clustering recovers missing views from observed data and ignores settings where missing sample-view entries can be acquired at a cost under a limited budget.
d6WB03h2qI.method: EAA first checks whether the observations in each view support reliable entry-level probabilistic modeling. With sufficient observations it acquires the entries with the highest conditional information gain about the latent cluster assignment; otherwise it selects views by residuals and samples eligible missing entries uniformly within them, updating the model after each acquisition.
d6WB03h2qI.key_idea: Match acquisition granularity to the evidence: score entries by conditional information gain on cluster assignment when observations suffice, else fall back to residual-based view selection with uniform sampling.
d6WB03h2qI.evidence: Experiments on multiple datasets (not named in the visible abstract) compare acquisition strategies under the same initial masks, budget (for example 30%) and final clustering step, with other IMVC methods converted into acquisition scores.
d6WB03h2qI.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says EAA effectively allocates limited budgets and improves clustering but the numbers are cut off.
d6WB03h2qI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that acquiring rather than only recovering missing views is a new and practical setting, and one notes the experimental protocol is fair with identical masks, budget and final clustering.
d6WB03h2qI.main_concern: The method assumes a known number of clusters K, noise-free acquired entries and given feature types, and its information-gain score is not directly validated against true clustering benefit.

F10Q8H9F7A.one_liner: Exactly invertible flow-map generative models with exact likelihoods and few-step sampling, trained via pointwise and distributional consistency.
F10Q8H9F7A.problem: Diffusion, flow matching and few-step flow-map generators have limited access to explicit model densities, unlike the normalizing flows and autoregressive models they evolved from.
F10Q8H9F7A.method: NFMs are exactly invertible pushforward maps that learn the integrator of an underlying dynamical system and give exact likelihoods by construction. They are trained with two self-distillation consistency objectives: pointwise matching (l2 flow-map-style regression) and distributional matching of pushforward distributions to marginals of a prescribed forward process.
F10Q8H9F7A.key_idea: Parameterize the integrator of a dynamical system as an exactly invertible map, then train it with pointwise l2 consistency and distributional matching to the marginals of a forward process.
F10Q8H9F7A.evidence: Conditional image generation on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-64, likelihood-based RLHF (KL-regularized REINFORCE), and equilibrium sampling with single-system and transferable Boltzmann Generators.
F10Q8H9F7A.claimed_gains: Claims the best sample quality among parameter-matched normalizing flows on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-64 while supporting likelihood-based RLHF; the Boltzmann Generator results are cut off in the truncated abstract.
F10Q8H9F7A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the goal of combining direct generation with tractable densities well motivated, with demonstrated uses in RL post-training and Boltzmann-generator sampling and broad evaluation.
F10Q8H9F7A.main_concern: The best image results (NFM-R) are numerically non-invertible, and restoring invertibility needs noise annealing and FP64 inference with worse FID, so no single variant delivers both top sample quality and exact likelihoods.

O3hOmH8X9s.one_liner: Scales auto-research loops over many environments to discover four token-saving mechanisms for coding-agent harnesses.
O3hOmH8X9s.problem: Unattended coding agents produce long trajectories of reasoning, tool use and feedback, so token cost limits scaling recursive self-improvement at the harness layer.
O3hOmH8X9s.method: SoL-Pi runs auto-research loops over increasingly numerous and diverse environments for harness rollouts, and four mechanisms survive selection: action execution, context compaction, observation handling and delegated reading. It builds on the Pi harness.
O3hOmH8X9s.key_idea: Run automated harness search across many diverse environments and keep only mechanisms that survive selection and transfer beyond the development setting.
O3hOmH8X9s.evidence: 51-task EdgeBench evaluation with GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 5 against Pi-baseline and native Codex and Claude Code harnesses, plus Terminal-Bench 4 held-out results and a multi-agent setting reported by reviewers.
O3hOmH8X9s.claimed_gains: Comparable performance to Pi-baseline while reducing recorded token traffic by 44.7-49.0% and API cost by about one third, with estimated hourly savings of $8.75-13.50 versus native harnesses and $4.36-5.71 versus Pi-baseline.
O3hOmH8X9s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically important and the mechanisms are concrete and reusable, with evaluation across several benchmarks and model backends and a roughly one-third API-cost reduction on both GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 5.
O3hOmH8X9s.main_concern: Efficiency is not free (about 94% of Pi-baseline EdgeBench score retained and Terminal-Bench 4 solved tasks fall from 18 to 15), and the contribution of the auto-research process over prior harness-evolution work such as Meta-Harness and DGM is not isolated.

qgA8X4m7cz.one_liner: Width bounds N+1 (RMSNorm) and N+2 (LayerNorm) for normalized shallow networks to approximate a given MLP.
qgA8X4m7cz.problem: Normalization layers depend on their inputs and stay nonlinear at inference, so placing RMSNorm or LayerNorm next to an activation may change the function a network can represent.
qgA8X4m7cz.method: Treats RMSNorm as input-dependent scaling and uses width augmentation to locally linearize normalization on compact feature sets, analyzing activation-normalized and preactivation-normalized shallow networks that approximate a width-N one-hidden-layer MLP. It proves upper bounds with error rates, matching worst-case lower bounds for fixed ReLU and tanh, and transfers universal-approximation results.
qgA8X4m7cz.key_idea: Augment width so normalization is locally linear on compact feature sets, letting a normalized network reproduce a target MLP with one extra unit (RMSNorm) or two (LayerNorm).
qgA8X4m7cz.evidence: Constructive proofs and lower bounds across activation- and preactivation-normalized settings, plus numerical experiments on synthetic one-dimensional functions with explicitly constructed networks that recover the predicted rates in all five settings.
qgA8X4m7cz.claimed_gains: Widths N+1 (RMSNorm) and N+2 (LayerNorm) are worst-case optimal for fixed ReLU in both modes and fixed tanh in affine PN mode, with error O(r^-1) at width N+r for AN networks with any continuous nonconstant activation.
qgA8X4m7cz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the constructive, rigorous analysis systematic across normalization types and activation conditions, with quantitative upper bounds and sharp lower bounds on the extra width.
qgA8X4m7cz.main_concern: Results cover only one-hidden-layer networks with a single normalization and rely on large augmentation, so their relevance to deep trained networks is unclear, and the relative-approximation question itself needs stronger justification.

ZbCrgKZiAL.one_liner: Benchmark of 288 synthetic cases testing whether agent memory systems leak sensitive relations by joining clues across sessions.
ZbCrgKZiAL.problem: Agents with long-term memory can combine individually harmless records across sessions and state a sensitive relation while doing an ordinary task, and attribute-visibility checks alone miss this.
ZbCrgKZiAL.method: MemJoin supplies 288 synthetic cases where the full history entails a sensitive relation but every single session is insufficient, and evaluates six memory systems plus full-history and no-history controls with the same answer-generating model. It separately checks which target attribute values appear in stored records and retrieved context and whether the final answer states the complete person-linked relation.
ZbCrgKZiAL.key_idea: Build cases where only the combination of sessions reveals a relation, then separate attribute visibility in memory from complete person-linked relation output, with broken-link controls.
ZbCrgKZiAL.evidence: Six memory systems with one reader model (Qwen 3.5 9B according to reviewers), full-history and no-history controls, and a paired test on a prespecified subset where removing shared identifiers changes complete-relation output.
ZbCrgKZiAL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard cross-session privacy as a timely problem and the benchmark as carefully constructed, with full-history, isolated-session and broken-link validations and useful comparisons across six memory frameworks.
ZbCrgKZiAL.main_concern: Evaluation uses a single 9B non-thinking reader model with automated judging and no reported human agreement, so generalization of the findings to other models is unclear.

Pu4KeVlW6o.one_liner: Multi-view clustering that uses MLLM-derived semantic seeds to guide merge-split corrections of a geometric partition.
Pu4KeVlW6o.problem: Geometric consistency alone does not ensure semantic correctness in multi-view clustering: nuisance variation can fragment one class across clusters and shared contextual cues can mix distinct classes.
Pu4KeVlW6o.method: SemReC starts from a geometric partition, extracts semantic descriptions of sparse, coverage-oriented representatives with a multimodal LLM, and organizes them into frozen semantic seeds. The seeds guide split proposals, and a joint geometric-semantic objective evaluates coupled merge-split moves that preserve the cluster count.
Pu4KeVlW6o.key_idea: Freeze MLLM-generated semantic seeds from sparse representatives, then accept coupled merge-split moves only if a joint geometric-semantic objective improves, keeping the cluster count fixed.
Pu4KeVlW6o.evidence: Four benchmarks spanning visual, image-text and audio-text settings (including Caltech and AwA2 per reviewers), compared against baselines, with ablations of the entropy terms.
Pu4KeVlW6o.claimed_gains: Average ACC of 84.97% and the highest ACC on all four datasets among the compared baselines.
Pu4KeVlW6o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the distinction between semantic fragmentation and mixing a coherent motivation for joint merging and splitting, and note the highest ACC on all four benchmarks.
Pu4KeVlW6o.main_concern: Presentation and attribution are weak: one reviewer cites inconsistent stage descriptions, undefined notation and poor organization, and another finds it unclear which component is the main algorithmic innovation beyond integrating MLLM extraction, graph regularization and merge-split optimization.

CY2WP2TjuS.one_liner: Benchmark of 300 prompts evaluating visual text rendering in video generation, plus a director-agent refinement framework.
CY2WP2TjuS.problem: Video generation benchmarks measure visual quality, aesthetics and physical plausibility but largely ignore whether text appearing in generated scenes is rendered correctly.
CY2WP2TjuS.method: VTR-Bench places text in application scenarios such as advertisements and scientific videos (300 prompts, five scenario categories) with an automated, human-aligned pipeline that scores text fidelity by carrier-specific transcription and scene and motion requirements by a prompt-specific chain of queries. A Keyframe-Guided Agentic Framework has a Director agent coordinate image and video generation with visual evaluation to refine outputs and select candidates.
CY2WP2TjuS.key_idea: Score text fidelity by carrier-specific transcription separately from prompt-specific scene and motion checks, and use a director agent with keyframe visual feedback to iteratively refine and select generations.
CY2WP2TjuS.evidence: Experiments on 11 video generation models (abstract truncated afterward), with human validation by three annotators on 100 videos and 1202 text blocks bound to concrete carriers reported by reviewers.
CY2WP2TjuS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a real gap by separating text accuracy from scene quality, covering multiple carriers and long passages, with careful construction and informative failure analysis.
CY2WP2TjuS.main_concern: Evaluation validity is limited: the same VLM family does scoring and transcription with no cross-evaluator test, human validation covers only models with readable text, and the agentic framework is tested on one model without ablations.

jPGGmOF9j3.one_liner: Rule-based generation of music-editing instruction data and a studio-tool toolkit for training agentic music post-production.
jPGGmOF9j3.problem: Music generation models produce one-shot output but cannot do the fine-grained iterative refinement of post-production, and existing corpora do not map realistic production chains onto the vocabulary musicians use.
jPGGmOF9j3.method: RIME generates paired edit-instruction data from any baseline music dataset using canonical methods, design patterns and constraints derived from real production workflows, relying on POEMS, a toolkit combining stem separation, mixing and common studio effects. The framework also covers fine-tuning and evaluation, with instructions at three abstraction levels (AL0-AL2) per reviewers.
jPGGmOF9j3.key_idea: Compile realistic effect chains from production-derived rule recipes into paired instruction-edit data at three abstraction levels, executed through a tool library of separation, mixing and effects.
jPGGmOF9j3.evidence: Agents evaluated on generated data with SFT comparisons, audio metrics (FAD, KAD, MERT similarity) and a listening study (n=10) validating instruction matching, per reviewers; the abstract is truncated before the results.
jPGGmOF9j3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the musician-centered iterative post-production task well motivated and the data pipeline carefully built, with an audited recipe set, LLM-judge screening and a listening study.
