jPGGmOF9j3.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited and the evaluation is weak: it mostly integrates existing audio tools with standard SFT, audio metrics lack a do-nothing reference, and AL2 is scored against a single reference effect graph rather than perceptual success.

u66OToCNB2.one_liner: Dense VLA RL rewards derived from signal temporal logic specifications that an LLM generates offline from instructions.
u66OToCNB2.problem: RL fine-tuning of vision-language-action models relies on sparse binary rewards, while LLM-generated or VLM-evaluated dense rewards are inefficient and can be unreliable.
u66OToCNB2.method: An LLM-aided offline step converts language instructions into STL specifications over task-level atomic propositions. During execution, a privileged-state or lightweight visual grounding module evaluates proposition satisfaction, and a runtime monitor aggregates quantitative values along the specification's temporal structure into dense rewards.
u66OToCNB2.key_idea: Compute rewards from the quantitative semantics of STL specifications, evaluating atomic propositions with state or visual grounding and aggregating them with a runtime monitor.
u66OToCNB2.evidence: Simulated LIBERO experiments (LIBERO-Goal and LIBERO-Long highlighted by reviewers) with privileged-state and visual variants against sparse-reward and Text2Reward baselines, plus qualitative real-world reward curves; the abstract is truncated before results.
u66OToCNB2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value that the rewards are interpretable and traceable to explicit conditions, avoid LLM-as-judge unreliability, and that the lightweight visual variant trains faster than VLM-evaluator baselines.
u66OToCNB2.main_concern: It is unclear whether gains come from the specification framework or from hand-designed margins, tuned thresholds and human-corrected specifications, and the real-world claim rests on qualitative reward curves with all RL training done in simulation.

4SSsoBBN42.one_liner: End-to-end 3D/4D geometric foundation model decoding entity masks with learnable global object queries instead of clustering.
4SSsoBBN42.problem: Instance-grounded geometric foundation models decode entities through hyperparameter-sensitive clustering, making masks unreliable and costly, and inherit the low native resolution of geometry transformers.
4SSsoBBN42.method: Entity3R extracts high-resolution geometry-instance features with a dual-branch backbone and decodes 3D/4D-consistent entity masks with learnable global object queries that interact with frame-level instance features. A training-free chunk-wise decoding strategy handles more entities than the query budget and longer sequences, and training uses EntityWorld, a corpus of 360K sequences and 84.8M frames with automatically annotated masklets.
4SSsoBBN42.key_idea: Replace post-hoc clustering with global object queries interacting with frame-level instance features from a high-resolution dual-branch backbone, decoded chunk-wise at inference.
4SSsoBBN42.evidence: Segmentation and geometry benchmarks including DAVIS and VIPSeg compared against EntitySAM and DAGE-based baselines, with ablations of the high-resolution branch, query placement and chunking; the abstract is truncated before results.
4SSsoBBN42.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; a reviewer reports 78.9 DAVIS J&F and 71.2 VIPSeg VEQ versus 71.4 and 61.4 for EntitySAM.
4SSsoBBN42.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it gives strong segmentation gains over compared methods at low decoding cost while keeping competitive geometry, and that the unified system and the large EntityWorld corpus are practically useful.
4SSsoBBN42.main_concern: Gains are not disentangled: the new decoder is confounded with a stronger backbone initialization, a high-resolution DINOv3 encoder and the new EntityWorld data, and novelty over DAGE and Mask2Former-style designs is limited.

KskpeXIMbk.one_liner: Executable benchmark of 95 seismic data-processing tasks and an SFT-plus-RL trained LLM agent for it.
KskpeXIMbk.problem: Existing agent benchmarks seldom combine executable multi-turn interaction with task-specific evaluation of scientific data products such as seismic processing pipelines.
KskpeXIMbk.method: SeisAgentBench has 95 tasks across 19 processing families, scored by deterministic family-specific seismic diagnostics, compatible reference agreement, artifact-preservation checks and workflow cost. SeisAgent is an LLM policy specialized through trajectory-level supervised learning followed by group-relative RL post-training.
KskpeXIMbk.key_idea: Score agents on the scientific quality and signal preservation of produced seismic artifacts via deterministic diagnostics, and train a policy with trajectory-level SFT then group-relative RL.
KskpeXIMbk.evidence: Six models from several families evaluated zero-shot and after SFT and RL on held-out tasks from the same processing families, per reviewers; the abstract itself reports no results.
KskpeXIMbk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is useful because it evaluates artifact-level scientific quality and signal preservation rather than task completion alone, with executable tools forming a gym-like environment.
KskpeXIMbk.main_concern: Benchmark difficulty and generalization are questioned: zero-shot Qwen3-14B already reaches 94.7% valid completion, no frontier model is evaluated, test tasks share families with training, and the contribution is seen as integrating existing agent and SFT-RL techniques.

hShILxckIE.one_liner: Feed-forward 4D reconstruction and 3D point tracking from arbitrary image sets using order-invariant, ID-based queries.
hShILxckIE.problem: Dynamic scenes captured by a moving camera, multiple streams or images at different times need correspondence across viewpoints, capture times and visibility changes without assuming an input ordering.
hShILxckIE.method: ARROW is a feed-forward model that unifies 3D reconstruction and 3D point tracking over arbitrary image sets, using order-invariant querying that associates queries with observations through content-derived IDs rather than index-based embeddings. It is trained on more diverse input sets, including non-sequential sampling across time and camera views and static and dynamic data.
hShILxckIE.key_idea: Condition queries on content-derived observation IDs instead of order-dependent index embeddings, and train on diverse unordered sets of views and times.
hShILxckIE.evidence: Evaluated on 3D tracking (WorldTrack, TAPVid-3D), an adapted RGB-only MVTracker multi-view tracking benchmark and 3D reconstruction tasks, with an index-based versus ID-based querying comparison.
hShILxckIE.claimed_gains: Claims the best results on WorldTrack and TAPVid-3D tracking and outperforms dedicated multi-view trackers on the adapted MVTracker benchmark while staying competitive in reconstruction; no numeric margins are stated.
hShILxckIE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method clearly presented and motivated, with thorough evaluation and clear gains on public tracking benchmarks, and value the unified framework for reconstruction and monocular and multi-view tracking.
hShILxckIE.main_concern: The novelty of order-invariant querying is questioned because related methods (V-DPM, 4RC) already use similar components, and runtime analysis against them is missing.

h3YaEFUWBn.one_liner: Shows pool geometry changes the value of adaptive acquisition in noisy binary affine prediction via Bayes Brier risk limits.
h3YaEFUWBn.problem: It is unclear how the geometry of the available query pool affects the benefit of adaptive versus fixed label acquisition under a fixed budget.
h3YaEFUWBn.method: Studies two regions, one following a uniformly drawn noisy binary affine rule and one with independent fair labels, and derives limiting Bayes Brier risks for fixed, two-batch and fully adaptive acquisition on uniform random pools versus a structured prescribed-subcube pool. The lower bound combines uniform early-evidence control with prediction bounds at outcome-dependent counts, and the structured policy uses o(r) verification labels before recovery.
h3YaEFUWBn.key_idea: On uniform random pools all acquisition classes share one limiting risk, while a structured subcube pool lets two batches verify the signal region with o(r) labels first.
h3YaEFUWBn.evidence: Theoretical results (limiting Bayes Brier risk, lower bounds against arbitrary adaptive policies, finite-risk separation inequalities under positive noise) supported by exact acquisition studies and paired experiments.
h3YaEFUWBn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question of how pool geometry affects adaptive acquisition interesting and the exact asymptotic characterization, with lower bounds for arbitrary adaptive policies, nontrivial.
h3YaEFUWBn.main_concern: The setting is specialized and somewhat artificial (noisy binary affine rules with known regional structure and noise rates, unrestricted computation), and the presentation is hard to access for readers outside the area.

oC7CcoLUcL.one_liner: Single-pass failure predictor for VLA models using separate alignment, reasoning and decoding uncertainty scores.
oC7CcoLUcL.problem: Existing VLA failure detectors return one score for the whole policy and cannot say whether a failure originates in scene-instruction alignment, reasoning or action decoding.
oC7CcoLUcL.method: The paper proves an exact decomposition of predictive action entropy into alignment, reasoning and decoding terms with nonnegative population values, and that failure predictability decomposes into nonnegative gains from phase-restricted scores. STAGE extracts alignment and reasoning signals from stage representations, computes decoding uncertainty from the decoder and combines the three to predict failure in one VLA forward pass.
oC7CcoLUcL.key_idea: Split a VLA step into alignment, reasoning and decoding phases and score failure risk from each phase's representation or decoder uncertainty, combined in a single forward pass.
oC7CcoLUcL.evidence: Experiments on three VLA families (OpenVLA, pi0, pi0-FAST), four LIBERO suites and SimplerEnv, with real-robot rollouts and seen and unseen task splits per reviewers.
oC7CcoLUcL.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest AUROC in most settings across the evaluated VLA families and benchmarks; the numeric values are cut off in the truncated abstract.
oC7CcoLUcL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the stage-wise formulation well motivated and the design simple and effective, needing one pass of the frozen VLA and no stage-level supervision, with evaluation across three VLA families and decoder types.
oC7CcoLUcL.main_concern: Stage attribution is weakly validated: the theory covers optimal log-linear probes rather than STAGE's learned scores, and attribution is never used in an intervention or shown to beat a holistic score in closed loop.

m3eJrKoGzl.one_liner: LM-driven evolutionary and agentic search discovers sampling functions yielding hard relational reasoning instances for an Edge Transformer.
m3eJrKoGzl.problem: It is unclear what makes relational reasoning instances hard, which hampers evaluating systematic generalization to instances harder than those seen in training.
m3eJrKoGzl.method: Given a world parametrized by Datalog rules and an Edge Transformer as reasoning evaluator, the authors use FunSearch-based LM-driven evolutionary search and autonomous agentic search to discover sampling functions that yield hard instances. They then retrain the Edge Transformer on this data and apply the same machinery to novel worlds proposed by LMs.
m3eJrKoGzl.key_idea: Treat benchmark generation as adversarial search: language models write sampler programs whose fitness is the evaluator's failure, with entailments verified automatically by a solver.
m3eJrKoGzl.evidence: Cross-evaluation tables of discovered samplers (evolutionary, agentic and Claude-designed) against Edge Transformers trained on other sampler distributions, on small knowledge graphs with at most eight entities.
m3eJrKoGzl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find framing benchmark generation as adversarial sampling against a reasoner interesting, with automatically verifiable targets and discovered samplers that expose difficulty not explained by standard metrics such as inference depth.
m3eJrKoGzl.main_concern: The evidence does not isolate the value of LLM-guided search from a matched non-LLM search baseline, and experiments use only small instances, leaving scalability unclear.

rRU85cpmNt.one_liner: Two-stage SFT then annotation-free RL post-training of a 9B LLM to write 3D primitive-assembly programs from text.
rRU85cpmNt.problem: Open-ended text-conditioned primitive assembly is underexplored because existing approaches depend on reference geometry or paired supervision over predefined component vocabularies.
rRU85cpmNt.method: PrimLLM conditions a 9B open-weight LLM on dense captions from component planning, first learning program syntax and component-to-geometry mappings with Structure-Aware SFT. Annotation-Free RL then improves assembly with rule-based rewards for program validity and physical plausibility plus vision-language-model feedback on multi-view renderings, keeping the generation policy text-only.
rRU85cpmNt.key_idea: Use VLM feedback on multi-view renders of executed primitive programs as an RL reward, combined with rule-based validity and plausibility rewards, so no program annotations are needed.
rRU85cpmNt.evidence: Comparisons with baselines including frontier LLMs and the base generator using GPT-based semantic-alignment and VQA evaluation, with training-stage ablations and a human check of the visual reward per reviewers; the abstract is truncated before results.
rRU85cpmNt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider the task useful because primitive programs give an editable representation, find the SFT-then-RL stages well motivated, and see a clear improvement over the base generator.
rRU85cpmNt.main_concern: Evidence for the reward-based training and for superiority over the strongest baseline is weak: gains are not separated from external planning and program scaffolding, the margin over the top baseline is tiny, and code and full reward and baseline settings are not provided.

U4w0JRRgaP.one_liner: Open-source full stack scaling dexterous VLA pretraining from 9,606 hours of curated egocentric human video.
U4w0JRRgaP.problem: Learning dexterous manipulation from expert demonstrations demands massive real-world data, which is prohibitively expensive for high-dimensional, data-scarce dexterous hands.
U4w0JRRgaP.method: The system combines EgoSmith, a pipeline curating in-the-wild egocentric video into 9,606 hours of pre-training data, a Robot Stack for teleoperation and human-in-the-loop correction on dexterous hands, and EgoSteer, a world-model-enhanced VLA on a morphology-aligned action space. Human-data pre-training gives language-guided priors that robot post-training grounds and DAgger refines.
U4w0JRRgaP.key_idea: Pretrain a world-model-enhanced VLA on egocentric human video in a morphology-aligned action space, then ground it with robot post-training and DAgger corrections.
U4w0JRRgaP.evidence: Real-robot experiments on 45 tasks (including unseen tasks, compositional generalization and instruction switching) and few-shot adaptation to five long-horizon tasks on two embodiments, with comparisons to pi0.5 and Being-H0.5 per reviewers.
U4w0JRRgaP.claimed_gains: EgoSmith has 8.3x higher throughput and better accuracy than prior SOTA, and the pre-trained model few-shot adapts to five long-horizon tasks on two embodiments with 79% average progress.
U4w0JRRgaP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the system is comprehensive and practically valuable, spanning data processing, policy learning and deployment, with extensive real-robot evaluation and open release of code and checkpoints.
U4w0JRRgaP.main_concern: The contribution is mainly integration of existing techniques (flow matching, future-feature prediction, DAgger, RTC), and baseline and scaling experiments are confounded so the source of the gains is hard to isolate.

EZX32RpU95.one_liner: Diffusion framework controlling external 9-DoF pose and internal structure of multiple objects from two 2D geometric maps.
EZX32RpU95.problem: In scenes with several open-category objects, controls for placement, orientation and internal articulation are rarely available together in controllable image generation.
EZX32RpU95.method: PoseStage conditions generation on two 2D geometric maps for external pose and internal structure, and handles reference-guided generation and editing at inference by extending the input sequence of a model trained only on standard conditional generation. A training-free instance-routing mask removes direct attention between instances to reduce attribute mixing, and a hybrid real and synthetic dataset supplies aligned annotations.
EZX32RpU95.key_idea: Condition a diffusion model on both an external-pose map and an internal-structure map, and mask attention between instances at inference so each object's appearance and text stay separate.
EZX32RpU95.evidence: A newly built hybrid real and synthetic dataset and a benchmark evaluating both controls, with comparisons to SceneDesigner and other methods and ablations of the control maps and inference-time routing.
EZX32RpU95.claimed_gains: Outperforms existing methods on the authors' benchmark; the abstract gives no numbers, though a reviewer cites angular error 26.93 versus 57.53 and structural F1 0.868 versus 0.521 for SceneDesigner.
EZX32RpU95.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the combined control of placement, orientation, articulation and appearance useful, the approach simple and training-free for editing and reference tasks, and the ablations and results convincing.
EZX32RpU95.main_concern: The source of improvement is unclear because baselines differ in backbone, data and inputs, and the novelty over SceneDesigner, SeeThrough3D and BoxCtrl (adding skeleton conditioning and an existing attention mask) is seen as incremental.

gSeqIWO7wy.one_liner: Benchmark and post-training (orbit-grouped GRPO with a frame-canonical reward) for panoramic VLMs under yaw rotation.
gSeqIWO7wy.problem: Panoramic VLMs can show stable average accuracy while giving stale-frame predictions that keep the previous viewpoint's answer instead of reasoning in the current reference frame after the agent turns.
gSeqIWO7wy.method: YawOrbit-Bench applies pixel-preserving yaw rotations and separates viewpoint-invariant from equivariant questions with geometry-regenerated targets. OrbitAlign post-trains with geometry-grounded orbit supervision, orbit-grouped GRPO and a correctness-gated Frame-Canonical Orbit (FCO) reward.
gSeqIWO7wy.key_idea: Reward answers only when correct in the current frame across all yaw rotations of the same image, grouping rotated variants in GRPO and gating the FCO reward by correctness.
gSeqIWO7wy.evidence: Evaluation of open-weight and hosted API VLMs on YawOrbit-Bench, and OrbitAlign trained across four backbones with ablations against PanoEnv GRPO.
gSeqIWO7wy.claimed_gains: Hosted models reach only 35.12--53.72% full-orbit accuracy, and FCO further reduces stale predictions by 12.13 percentage points in the ablation, with OrbitAlign improving changed-label accuracy over PanoEnv GRPO across four backbones.
gSeqIWO7wy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the benchmark well motivated and carefully designed, with pixel-preserving rotations and correctness-versus-consistency metrics that expose failures hidden by average accuracy.
gSeqIWO7wy.main_concern: Most gains come from SFT on regenerated targets while the RL components add little (FCO adds about two points and slightly lowers E1 accuracy), the base models are dated, and evaluation is limited to relative-position questions under the same relation rule used in training.

6inpXQUf97.one_liner: Counterfactual step rewards for sequential diagnosis RL, comparing chosen examinations against alternatives via short rollouts.
6inpXQUf97.problem: Outcome-only rewards in sequential diagnosis RL cause reward blindness, where paths of different efficiency score the same, and credit dilution, where one final score is spread over all steps.
6inpXQUf97.method: CoSteP selects decision-critical states where the policy is uncertain and compares the chosen action with plausible counterfactual alternatives using short rollouts and a utility combining diagnostic accuracy and examination cost. A persistent rollout cache reuses compatible trajectories across training batches, avoiding expert step annotations and a learned critic.
6inpXQUf97.key_idea: At high-uncertainty states, price each action by short-rollout utility of accuracy and examination cost relative to alternative actions, reusing cached rollouts, to give annotation-free step rewards.
6inpXQUf97.evidence: Experiments on MIMIC-IV, ClinicalBench and a private dataset (abstract truncated), with source code attached in the supplement per reviewers.
6inpXQUf97.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree sequential diagnosis under examination-cost constraints is a meaningful problem and that comparing the selected examination with alternatives is a well-motivated way to build action-sensitive rewards.
6inpXQUf97.main_concern: The counterfactual rollouts are policy- and simulator-dependent utility comparisons rather than causal estimates, step rewards are still aggregated to trajectory level, and novelty beyond uncertainty-based state selection and rollout caching is unclear.

fEl9WoRoiP.one_liner: Online class-prior tracking from positive and unlabeled source data, with regret bounds separating temporal and finite-source error.
fEl9WoRoiP.problem: Existing online label-shift methods assume labeled source data from every class, and the statistical price of online adaptation when the source has no labeled negatives is unknown.
fEl9WoRoiP.method: Reconstructs the unobserved negative class from positive-unlabeled source data and tracks the changing target prior online, then derives a dynamic classification-regret bound for threshold adaptation against the best threshold of the same fixed score at each target prior. Lower bounds show both error terms are unavoidable in general.
fEl9WoRoiP.key_idea: Reconstructing the negative class from PU data keeps the temporal tracking rate and puts the PU cost into a finite-source error term whose weights depend on the target-prior path.
fEl9WoRoiP.evidence: Theorems with lower bounds under a source-sample stability condition, plus experiments (abstract truncated before details).
fEl9WoRoiP.claimed_gains: The temporal component of the cumulative squared prior-tracking error retains the O~(T^{1/3} V_T^{2/3}) dependence achieved with positive and negative source data.
fEl9WoRoiP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the separation of temporal tracking error from a path-dependent finite-source error insightful and strengthened by lower bounds, in a meaningful setting without labeled negatives.
fEl9WoRoiP.main_concern: Technical novelty is limited because the algorithm builds on known PU estimation and online regression (ALIGATOR), and the proofs largely combine concentration bounds with inherited results.

k3wyk4rkSr.one_liner: Claim-level video captioning rewards that verify decomposed visual claims against the video with reference-anchored credit.
k3wyk4rkSr.problem: Reward functions for dense video captioning assume reference captions cover all valid content, so they penalize correct visual details that a single reference omits.
k3wyk4rkSr.method: CuRe decomposes captions into visual claims such as entities and actions and verifies each against the video. Reference-matched claims get full credit, video-supported claims beyond the reference get bounded credit, and unsupported claims get zero credit; the reward is used for RL post-training and for re-captioning corpora.
k3wyk4rkSr.key_idea: Give full credit to reference-matched claims, bounded credit to video-verified claims beyond the reference, and zero credit to unsupported claims.
k3wyk4rkSr.evidence: Three public captioning benchmarks, plus re-captioning three video-caption corpora (867K samples) and pretraining VLMs on original versus CuRe-generated captions, with reward baselines such as Holistic and continued SFT per reviewers.
k3wyk4rkSr.claimed_gains: Strongest results among open-source models on three public captioning benchmarks and improved performance from CuRe-recaptioned data (867K samples re-captioned); the size of the gains is cut off.
k3wyk4rkSr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the claim-level formulation addresses a real limitation of strict reference matching and gives a reasonable balance between rewarding extra valid detail and penalizing unsupported claims.
k3wyk4rkSr.main_concern: Methodological novelty is moderate relative to existing decompose-and-verify approaches (AutoDQ, FaithScore), and reward quality depends on imperfect model-based claim verification (81.93% accuracy reported by a reviewer).

2mNqSlYgrm.one_liner: Few-shot, mask-free anomaly editing trained on pairs built by first inpainting real anomalies away.
2mNqSlYgrm.problem: Reference-based anomaly synthesis needs explicit masks, global synthesis harms normal-region fidelity, and mask-free editing needs aligned normal-anomaly pairs that are rarely available.
2mNqSlYgrm.method: AnomalyEditor first removes annotated anomalies from real images with an inpainter fine-tuned on normal images to get aligned pairs, then fine-tunes a pretrained editor to add the anomalies back from text instructions. At inference it generates anomalies without an input mask and leaves normal regions intact; the abstract also mentions an additional spatial component that is cut off.
2mNqSlYgrm.key_idea: Build aligned training pairs in reverse by inpainting anomalies into normal appearance, then train the forward editor to add anomalies back from text.
2mNqSlYgrm.evidence: Three industrial inspection benchmarks with downstream defect classification and ablations including a forward-only variant, with KID used for fidelity per reviewers.
2mNqSlYgrm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the reverse-to-forward pair construction simple and well motivated, solving the alignment bottleneck, with evaluation on three inspection benchmarks and ablations showing the constructed pairs matter.
2mNqSlYgrm.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited since it chains existing inpainting and editing models, and the validity of the reverse-generated pairs (boundary artifacts, residual cues) is not directly established.

YjC9f4K6kn.one_liner: Sequential GAIA2 and SWE-Bench Pro benchmarks for persistent agent sessions, plus Seq-RL training on multi-task rollouts.
YjC9f4K6kn.problem: Agents are evaluated one task at a time, yet deployed agents run in persistent sessions where history, memory, files and prior experience carry across tasks.
YjC9f4K6kn.method: Builds sequential variants of GAIA2 and SWE-Bench Pro in which agents solve up to 40 tasks in one persistent session, and analyzes traces. Sequential RL (Seq-RL) trains on persistent multi-task rollouts with fine-grained credit assignment.
YjC9f4K6kn.key_idea: Train on persistent multi-task rollouts with fine-grained credit assignment across the task sequence, so the agent learns to reuse prior context.
YjC9f4K6kn.evidence: Evaluations of Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek v4 Pro on sequences of up to 40 tasks, and Seq-RL trained only on GAIA2-style data disjoint from evaluation and tested zero-shot on SWE-Bench Pro against a single-task RL baseline.
YjC9f4K6kn.claimed_gains: DeepSeek v4 Pro loses 5.9 percentage points on average under persistence, agents use up to 60% fewer output tokens, and Python's share of tool calls on GAIA2 rises by up to 4x; the Seq-RL gains on SWE-Bench Pro are cut off.
YjC9f4K6kn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating agents in persistent sessions is a useful, realistic setting that reveals behavior changes invisible in single-task evaluation, with convincing results including cross-domain transfer of Seq-RL.
YjC9f4K6kn.main_concern: The sources of Seq-RL's gains are not isolated (higher compute than single-task RL, one seed per configuration, modest effect of removing credit assignment), and novelty over existing sequential benchmarks such as ChainWorld, EvaLearn and CL-Bench is questioned.

e4EvcTUOkN.one_liner: Shows shared cooldown state in LiteLLM lets one tenant's rejected requests deny others, and proposes tenant-scoped cooldown.
e4EvcTUOkN.problem: LLM gateways enforce per-tenant quotas but share deployment cooldown records, so one tenant's failures can restrict other tenants' access to serviceable deployments.
e4EvcTUOkN.method: Identifies two LiteLLM attacks: requests rejected at a key's RPM limit with caller-supplied deployment identifiers reach failure handling and redirect another tenant to fallback with zero upstream calls, and admitted traffic creates cooldown records that outlast backend recovery. The defense is an origin check blocking deployment updates from key RPM rejections plus tenant-scoped cooldown that keeps shared records for backend faults.
e4EvcTUOkN.key_idea: Attribute each failure to its origin and scope cooldown per tenant, so a tenant's own rejections cannot update shared deployment cooldown records.
e4EvcTUOkN.evidence: Experiments with authenticated proxies and self-hosted vLLM, including five paired four-worker runs and direct backend probes.
e4EvcTUOkN.claimed_gains: Tenant scoping reduces victim fallback after recovery from 54/60 to 0/60 across five paired four-worker runs, while increasing attempts against exhausted shared quotas.
e4EvcTUOkN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a practical cross-tenant isolation flaw, traced through source code and backed by direct backend probes that separate gateway-induced denial from true unavailability.
e4EvcTUOkN.main_concern: Reported numbers are inconsistent or unexplained (54/60 versus 41/60 fallbacks for what looks like the same setup, and recovery probes dropping from 35/40 to 13/40 under scoped cooldown after 500 errors), and the defense covers only some attacker-controlled failures.

OZ6JYRP75V.one_liner: Theory of non-monotone accuracy under vanishing initialization: accuracy rises, collapses, then recovers in deep linear networks.
OZ6JYRP75V.problem: Training loss alone does not reveal how classification accuracy evolves under small initialization, where accuracy can rise, drop and later recover before the loss has appreciably decayed.
OZ6JYRP75V.method: Documents the accuracy well in deep linear networks, ReLU MLPs on MNIST, CNNs on CIFAR-10 and synthetic tasks, and explains it with a three-stage mechanism of target-driven organization, a degeneracy bottleneck and later recruitment and recovery. Rigorous theory is developed for shallow and deep linear networks.
OZ6JYRP75V.key_idea: Early target-driven organization gives high accuracy at vanishing predictor scale, a degeneracy bottleneck then degrades it, and later recruitment restores it.
OZ6JYRP75V.evidence: Rigorous analysis of shallow and deep linear networks, including a synthetic task where accuracy provably goes to 100%, collapses to 0 and later recovers, with observations across architectures, losses and optimizers on MNIST and CIFAR-10.
OZ6JYRP75V.claimed_gains: not stated; the headline result is a proof that accuracy on a simple synthetic task rises to 100%, collapses to 0 and later recovers permanently to 100%.
OZ6JYRP75V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the accuracy-well phenomenon interesting and shown across several empirical setups, with a substantive theory covering depths L=1, L=2 and L>=3 and clean ablations such as bias presence and location.
OZ6JYRP75V.main_concern: Novelty and relevance are questioned: the mechanism relies on known small-initialization dynamics, the drop may be nearly automatic for a low-rank classifier, theory (whitened inputs) and experiments are only partly matched, and links to grokking and double descent are underdeveloped.

x3nwOH53T7.one_liner: Generates compact instance-adaptive prompt embeddings from visible context to feed frozen time-series foundation models.
x3nwOH53T7.problem: Longer histories improve time-series foundation models but raise inference cost substantially.
x3nwOH53T7.method: PaCTS generates a small set of continuous latent prompt tokens conditioned on the visible context, built from instance-specific global statistics and refined with segment-level temporal information. The prompt module is trained jointly across heterogeneous series and deployed with a frozen backbone.
x3nwOH53T7.key_idea: Compress visible history into a few learned prompt tokens, generated from global statistics through a low-rank generator and refined by segment-level cross-attention, for a frozen backbone.
x3nwOH53T7.evidence: Forecasting experiments across context lengths and model architectures, with Chronos-2 compared against full fine-tuning, LoRA, LayerNorm-only tuning, BitFit and linear probing, and GIFT-Eval evaluation per reviewers.
x3nwOH53T7.claimed_gains: With a shorter input context, achieves comparable or better accuracy than the same frozen backbone with double context at substantially lower inference cost, and stronger improvements and out-of-distribution generalization than weight-space adaptation; no numeric values in the abstract.
x3nwOH53T7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation practical and the prompt-generation design lightweight, keeping the backbone frozen while adding few parameters and reducing FLOPs, memory and latency.
x3nwOH53T7.main_concern: Novelty over existing prompt-learning and parameter-efficient methods is unclear, and the evaluation is questioned (supervised adaptation on GIFT-Eval training intervals undermines the zero-shot comparison, and the long-context replacement claim is not validated).

qKhSMUWbbO.one_liner: Depth-guided video-to-audio generation using a Depth ControlNet plus SPL and SPE losses for distance-consistent sound.
qKhSMUWbbO.problem: Video-to-audio models treat the auditory scene as spatially static and distance-agnostic, ignoring distance-dependent attenuation and spectral filtering.
qKhSMUWbbO.method: DepthFoley extracts metric depth trajectories with metric depth estimation and guides a pre-trained backbone through a Depth ControlNet, with a training-free object-wise inference strategy for multi-object scenes. Sound Pressure Level (SPL) and Spectrally Perceptual Energy (SPE) losses plus depth-informed regularization teach realistic decay trends, evaluated with the new DITC and DIGA metrics.
qKhSMUWbbO.key_idea: Steer a frozen V2A backbone with metric depth trajectories through a ControlNet and supervise level and spectral energy (SPL and SPE losses) to follow distance-dependent decay.
qKhSMUWbbO.evidence: Experiments with the new DITC and DIGA metrics, a 30-participant user study and comparisons with CAFA and a post-hoc gain baseline per reviewers; the abstract is truncated before results.
qKhSMUWbbO.claimed_gains: Claims superior spatial-acoustic alignment and strong zero-shot generalization (abstract truncated); a reviewer cites a spatial alignment rating of 4.18 versus 2.67 for CAFA, with FAD changing only from 7.20 to 7.35.
qKhSMUWbbO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree distance-aware sound is a valuable, overlooked direction and that the user study shows clearly better spatial consistency at only a small audio-quality cost.
qKhSMUWbbO.main_concern: The new DITC and DIGA metrics depend on estimated depth and noisy YouTube-style data, and baseline comparisons are confounded (a post-hoc gain baseline reaches similar DITC), so gains are hard to attribute.

dZZVPQGzQY.one_liner: Diffusion language models trained with one cross-entropy objective so valid solutions become absorbing, stable states.
dZZVPQGzQY.problem: Reasoning tasks need any correct solution rather than the training answer distribution, but diffusion language models are built to match distributions.
dZZVPQGzQY.method: Trains with a single cross-entropy objective to reconstruct valid solutions from corrupted inputs. Theory gives conditions on the corruption process under which valid solutions are absorbing states of the optimal model and repeated sampling reaches them with exponentially fast convergence, plus a probability gap between valid and invalid states usable as a stopping criterion.
dZZVPQGzQY.key_idea: Train denoising cross-entropy so valid solutions are absorbing states of the optimal model, then stop sampling when the model's stay probability signals a valid state.
dZZVPQGzQY.evidence: Unconditional generation of valid Sudoku grids and program synthesis trained on TinyGSM and evaluated on GSM8K, with theory under conditions on the corruption process.
dZZVPQGzQY.claimed_gains: On GSM8K the model achieves 63.6% accuracy, comparable to 63.3% for the autoregressive greedy baseline.
dZZVPQGzQY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the distinction between distribution matching and finding any valid solution insightful, with clear theory linking token-level denoising cross-entropy to identifying valid candidates and strong results on Sudoku and GSM8K.
dZZVPQGzQY.main_concern: Empirical scope is narrow (Sudoku and GSM8K), matching autoregressive accuracy needs about 1024 model calls and noise annealing because direct categorical sampling fails, and the value of adaptive stopping is not demonstrated.

xu80Sc1btb.one_liner: Controlled test of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis using eight Hamiltonian systems rendered as video and text.
xu80Sc1btb.problem: Evidence for the Platonic Representation Hypothesis compares models only with each other because the true structure of natural images and text is unknown, so it cannot test convergence to the world or manipulate the cause of agreement.
xu80Sc1btb.method: Builds eight Hamiltonian systems with ground-truth latent variables h, rendered independently as video and text, and trains matched pairs of unshared encoders that differ only in prediction targets. It defines the H-subspace on which both latents carry the same linear statistics of h, proves alignment on it and shows a single linear map transports information between the spaces.
xu80Sc1btb.key_idea: Manipulate which targets each encoder predicts in a world with known latents, showing alignment arises only when both predict information about h, characterized by a shared H-subspace.
xu80Sc1btb.evidence: Controlled experiments on eight Hamiltonian systems with matched encoder pairs, a theorem on the H-subspace, and experiments with frozen pretrained models per reviewers.
xu80Sc1btb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the controlled setting with known ground-truth physics and manipulable supervision an important, carefully designed way to test the hypothesis, with extensive experiments.
xu80Sc1btb.main_concern: The simulated worlds are simple and the models may lack the scale and competence of the PRH regime, so extrapolating to natural data is unsafe, and the theory describes an existing correspondence rather than how training produces alignment.

Dmtlofg7tK.one_liner: Generalized chunk-wise parallel algorithm and kernels for training linear transformers with block-diagonal state transitions at 7B scale.
Dmtlofg7tK.problem: Block-diagonal state-transition matrices could increase the expressivity of linear transformers, but the lack of an adequate training algorithm has restricted them to small scales or specific block families.
Dmtlofg7tK.method: Develops a generalized chunk-wise parallel algorithm with hardware-aware kernels that lifts these restrictions, and uses it to train a Block-diagonal Gated Linear Transformer (BGLT) at 7B scale with a parameter-saving structure (cut off in the abstract). Reviewers note a Kronecker representation that avoids materializing full blocks and a local factorization that supports non-invertible gates.
Dmtlofg7tK.key_idea: Factorize block-diagonal transitions locally within chunks, using a Kronecker representation, so chunk-wise parallel training works for general, even non-invertible, blocks.
Dmtlofg7tK.evidence: Synthetic tasks including S5 length generalization and language modeling at 1.5B and 7B scale against KDA, with timing and memory measurements and ablations over optimizer, gate spectrum and seeds.
Dmtlofg7tK.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; reviewers report Delta-BGLT improving general and recall averages over KDA at 7B by 0.1 and 2.0 percentage points.
Dmtlofg7tK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the algorithm meaningfully expands the state-transition structures that can be trained efficiently in parallel, evaluated on synthetic tasks, 7B language modeling and detailed ablations.
Dmtlofg7tK.main_concern: Language-modeling gains over KDA are marginal and come with lower training throughput and larger memory, so a quality advantage at matched training cost is not established.

RZMgM79nrs.one_liner: Diffusion language models trained with a sequence-level alpha loss to keep parallel few-step predictions consistent.
RZMgM79nrs.problem: Reducing denoising steps makes discrete diffusion language models inconsistent because cross-entropy fits conditional token marginals while parallel generation requires consistent joint predictions.
RZMgM79nrs.method: AlphaDLM replaces cross-entropy with a sequence-level alpha loss that recovers cross-entropy as alpha goes to zero and has a joint-mode optimum at alpha one. The analysis shows how objective and factorization jointly set the fitted distribution and when intermediate alpha keeps multiple valid completions while excluding invalid token combinations.
RZMgM79nrs.key_idea: Train the factorized denoiser with a sequence-level alpha loss that interpolates between marginal cross-entropy and joint-mode fitting, removing invalid token combinations at few steps.
RZMgM79nrs.evidence: Trained on TinyGSM and evaluated on GSM8K, then scaled to the larger SDAR model (a 1.7B model per reviewers) on code and mathematics benchmarks.
RZMgM79nrs.claimed_gains: Achieves 34.6% accuracy on GSM8K with only four model evaluations when trained on TinyGSM.
RZMgM79nrs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see an elegant way to improve few-step generation through the training objective, with a matched comparison showing large gains at few evaluations and a larger-scale experiment beyond toy settings.
RZMgM79nrs.main_concern: Novelty and comparisons are limited: the alpha loss and most of the analysis come from prior work, there is no comparison with other few-step methods such as trajectory supervision or self-distillation, and experiments cover only math and code.

FqA1av3hjG.one_liner: Harnesses and a two-stage training framework that let models decide context allocation and reuse across windows for test-time scaling.
FqA1av3hjG.problem: Using extra test-time compute across multiple context windows requires deciding when to allocate fresh contexts and what to carry between them, which existing approaches prescribe in the harness rather than leaving to the model.
FqA1av3hjG.method: Hermes is a family of configurable harnesses that progressively varies model control over context allocation and reuse, and Hermes-Learn is a two-stage framework (SFT and RL per reviewers) that trains smaller models to use these capabilities. Training induces adaptive strategies that vary with the problem and the progress of reasoning.
FqA1av3hjG.key_idea: Shift context-allocation and reuse decisions from the harness to the model, then train it to choose among delegation strategies via SFT and RL.
FqA1av3hjG.evidence: Mathematics and science reasoning benchmarks across harness configurations and model families, with larger inference budgets than seen in training and comparisons against other test-time scaling baselines such as RSA.
FqA1av3hjG.claimed_gains: Claims the gains generalize across benchmarks and models, extrapolate beyond training-time inference compute and extend the accuracy-compute Pareto frontier over alternative baselines; no numbers in the abstract.
FqA1av3hjG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem of letting models manage contexts for test-time scaling clear and timely, with substantial gains under the Hermes harness across several benchmarks and model families.
FqA1av3hjG.main_concern: It is unclear whether training improves reasoning or only teaches use of the Hermes framework: inline accuracy drops on some benchmarks, an untrained base model with RSA nearly matches the trained result, and the benefit of choosing among strategies is not isolated.

2vvu4s8uw4.one_liner: Single-pass hallucination probe that removes the question-aligned direction from answer hidden states before classification.
2vvu4s8uw4.problem: Black-box consistency detectors need repeated inference, and single-pass white-box probes treat answer representations in isolation and degrade sharply under domain shift.
2vvu4s8uw4.method: QAoD projects the question-aligned direction out of the answer representation to get a question-orthogonal component, selects layers by diversity-penalized Fisher scoring and neurons by Fisher importance, and feeds the features to a lightweight probe. A joint probe pairs the orthogonal component with question context for in-domain accuracy, while an orthogonal-only probe supports cross-domain transfer.
2vvu4s8uw4.key_idea: Subtract the component of the answer hidden state aligned with the question, so the remaining question-orthogonal features predict correctness with less domain dependence.
2vvu4s8uw4.evidence: In-domain evaluation on TriviaQA, SQuAD, NQ and BioASQ and cross-domain tests including GSM8K, across several LLMs (16 model-dataset pairs per the TLDR).
2vvu4s8uw4.claimed_gains: Best in-domain AUROC on all 16 model-dataset pairs, up to 21% over the strongest white-box baseline in zero-shot OOD transfer, and competitive OOD performance at under 2% of generation cost.
2vvu4s8uw4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the focus on cross-domain generalization of hallucination detection worthwhile and the idea simple, inexpensive and conceptually minimal, with orthogonal-probe performance that stays stable under distribution shift.
2vvu4s8uw4.main_concern: Evaluation scope and rigor are questioned: only QA-style benchmarks and two OOD domains, F1 thresholds tuned on the evaluated split with unreported class imbalance, and strong related baselines such as CoCoA and LookBackLens are missing.

W15h4Z7T9s.one_liner: Cost-aware entropy-search acquisition function that picks experiments to reduce uncertainty in the hyperparameter scaling law itself.
W15h4Z7T9s.problem: Estimating optimal hyperparameter scaling laws for LLM training conventionally requires exhaustive grid searches over thousands of training runs.
W15h4Z7T9s.method: PLES builds on multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization with one GP shared across scales and, at each iteration, selects the configuration that maximally reduces scaling-law uncertainty per unit computational cost, which favors informative small-scale experiments. It also yields a natural stopping criterion from uncertainty.
W15h4Z7T9s.key_idea: Choose the next run by expected reduction in uncertainty of the fitted power law of per-scale optima, divided by compute cost, rather than optimizing a single objective.
W15h4Z7T9s.evidence: Synthetic benchmarks, surrogate models fitted to real LLM training data and actual LLM pre-training runs, compared against grid search, Sobol and Ladder BO baselines.
W15h4Z7T9s.claimed_gains: Converges to accurate optimal hyperparameter scaling laws using less than one-tenth of the computational budget required by conventional grid search and other baselines.
W15h4Z7T9s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practically important and the method principled and easy to follow, linking a cross-scale GP, per-scale optima and the power-law fit with a cost-aware acquisition and a natural stopping criterion.
W15h4Z7T9s.main_concern: Baselines and claims are questioned: the closest work (Li et al., 2026) and a multi-fidelity BO baseline are not compared, the 10% budget claim is ill-defined for real-LLM runs that share the same total budget, and LLM experiments fix D=20N.

kUYHO7k9wL.one_liner: Bayesian generative model for nonlinear instrumental-variable regression with a causally structured latent space and credible intervals.
kUYHO7k9wL.problem: Nonlinear IV methods struggle with high-dimensional covariates, operate in observed or generic learned feature spaces, and usually give point estimates without uncertainty quantification.
kUYHO7k9wL.method: BGM-IV performs posterior inference in a latent space that separates covariate variation by its role in the treatment and outcome mechanisms, and handles endogeneity with an IV-integrated pseudo-likelihood that averages over instrument-induced treatment variation. It outputs structural-function estimates with credible intervals.
kUYHO7k9wL.key_idea: Split covariate latents by their role in treatment versus outcome, and fit the outcome model with a pseudo-likelihood that averages over instrument-induced treatment variation.
kUYHO7k9wL.evidence: Benchmark datasets with 20 paired repetitions and a shared 10-restart budget for stochastic baselines, with interval coverage checked against the true structural function.
kUYHO7k9wL.claimed_gains: Outperforms existing nonlinear IV methods overall with significant gains in high-dimensional settings, and intervals cover the true structural function at or close to the nominal rate; no numbers in the abstract.
kUYHO7k9wL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the high-dimensional-covariate setting useful and the empirical evaluation careful, with identical training data across methods and equal restart budgets for stochastic baselines.
kUYHO7k9wL.main_concern: The uncertainty-quantification claim is weakly supported: the intervals are predictive intervals that omit uncertainty in the estimated structural function, and the causal justification of the tempered quasi-posterior and pseudo-likelihood is incomplete.

ui9dWlC6Uh.one_liner: Hybrid recurrent-attention language model that fires attention blocks only when output entropy exceeds a dynamic threshold.
ui9dWlC6Uh.problem: Recurrent-attention hybrids apply attention uniformly across positions even where the recurrent state alone suffices for accurate prediction.
ui9dWlC6Uh.method: AMOR augments a recurrent backbone (Mamba2 or Gated DeltaNet) with entropy-gated attention blocks that activate only when output entropy exceeds a threshold derived from a running batch median and scaled standard deviation. The binary gate needs no learned routing parameters, and keys and values are retained at skipped positions.
ui9dWlC6Uh.key_idea: Gate attention with a parameter-free binary rule comparing the model's own output entropy to a running median-plus-scaled-deviation threshold, instead of fixed attention layers.
ui9dWlC6Uh.evidence: Pretraining from scratch on FineWeb-Edu at multiple scales with Mamba2 and Gated DeltaNet backbones, evaluated on eight common-sense reasoning tasks, retrieval, long-context robustness under RoPE shift, and measured latency and memory against recurrent, attention and fixed-schedule hybrid baselines.
ui9dWlC6Uh.claimed_gains: With attention invoked on only ~40% of positions, one AMOR variant achieves the highest eight-task common-sense reasoning average at each scale among pure recurrent, pure attention and fixed-schedule hybrid models.
ui9dWlC6Uh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clearly written and the design simple and practical, with evaluation across scales, backbones and task families and consistent retrieval gains over pure recurrent models.
ui9dWlC6Uh.main_concern: Entropy as the routing signal is not justified or isolated: there is no adaptive or learned router baseline at matched firing rate, and added capacity relative to fixed-schedule hybrids is not controlled.

2Nap9BxV1E.one_liner: Training-free logit offsets that raise reference attention in edit regions and suppress it in keep regions of diffusion editors.
2Nap9BxV1E.problem: Reference-guided diffusion editors allocate little attention to the reference, so they fail to reproduce user-provided references faithfully.
2Nap9BxV1E.method: RefGAP measures reference-attention mass during the forward pass and sets per-layer logit-offset magnitudes online: positive offsets for edit-region queries strengthen reference usage, and negative offsets for keep-region queries limit changes outside the edit. Two global coefficients are chosen once on four development editors and held fixed.
2Nap9BxV1E.key_idea: Add logit offsets to reference keys, sized per layer by the measured reference-attention mass, positive for edit-region queries and negative for keep-region queries.
2Nap9BxV1E.evidence: Seven diffusion-based image and video editors on head swapping and face swapping (identity fidelity), with transfer tests on virtual try-on and background replacement, human evaluation across four tasks and a constant-bias comparison.
2Nap9BxV1E.claimed_gains: Improves identity fidelity in head and face swapping across seven editors (sometimes at higher pose error) and matches separately tuned constant edit-side biases without per-approach strength sweeps; no numbers given.
2Nap9BxV1E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the evidence for improved identity fidelity broad and statistically careful, with a simple training-free method that performs about as well as carefully tuned settings without per-editor adjustment.
2Nap9BxV1E.main_concern: The necessity and novelty of the mass-dependent correction are not established: a simple shared constant offset pair is not excluded, related attention-control methods are close, and results are mixed for background replacement with preservation costs in pose.

VKHqaZi1Aw.one_liner: Feed-forward crowd reconstruction from video using multi-joint height targets and global trajectory fusion for spatio-temporal consistency.
VKHqaZi1Aw.problem: Per-person video methods miss relative positions in a scene, crop-based crowd methods regress crop-dependent targets that jitter over time, and consistent methods need expensive per-sequence optimization.
VKHqaZi1Aw.method: StableCrowd predicts Multi-Joint Height, the metric height of every joint above the scene surface, which is crop-invariant, stable over time and can be lifted in closed form to metric 3D joints. Global Trajectory Fusion regresses the trajectory in the same space for sequences of any length, and each crop is warped to a canonical camera so close-range data can train for large scenes.
VKHqaZi1Aw.key_idea: Use the crop-invariant metric height of every joint above the scene surface as the localization target, and fuse per-joint estimates by regressing the trajectory in that same space.
VKHqaZi1Aw.evidence: Comparisons with recent methods on synthetic (VirtualCrowd) and real-world datasets, with ablations such as a MJH versus HVIP representation comparison; the abstract is truncated before results.
VKHqaZi1Aw.claimed_gains: Claims to be the first feed-forward method to achieve spatio-temporal consistency on large-scene video; the visible abstract gives no numbers.
VKHqaZi1Aw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important and Multi-Joint Height a natural, geometrically motivated crop-invariant target, with strong results against recent methods on synthetic and real data and a feed-forward pipeline that avoids per-sequence optimization.
VKHqaZi1Aw.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate the benefit of Multi-Joint Height from Global Trajectory Fusion (baselines lack the same temporal fusion), and the novelty of Canonical Camera Normalization over perspective crop layers is unclear.

iwYPSWfPlD.one_liner: Per-layer gradient clipping in a scale-calibrated preconditioned space for differentially private training.
iwYPSWfPlD.problem: Clipping each layer with its own threshold gives different scaling factors across layers, distorting the full-gradient direction and lowering utility in DP training.
iwYPSWfPlD.method: SCP-Clip scales gradients with a preconditioner built from historical private second moments, clips per layer in that space, then inverts the scaling, with a slack controller (per reviewers) calibrating the target. It adds no privacy cost and keeps per-layer clipping's memory efficiency, and a utility bound on private gradient estimation error is proven under stable feedback.
iwYPSWfPlD.key_idea: Scale, privatize, then invert: clip per layer in a preconditioned space calibrated by historical private second moments so per-layer scaling factors distort the gradient direction less.
iwYPSWfPlD.evidence: Pretrained RoBERTa-base and large on GLUE, ViT-small and large on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and GPT-2 and GPT-2 medium on E2E, compared with flat clipping and fixed, auto and adaptive per-layer clipping, plus memory and time overhead measurements.
iwYPSWfPlD.claimed_gains: Outperforms flat clipping in most settings, with accuracy gains of up to 4.28% over adaptive per-layer clipping.
iwYPSWfPlD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find it a practical improvement with a clean, exact privacy argument, retaining per-layer clipping's memory benefits with small overhead while closing most of the utility gap to flat clipping.
iwYPSWfPlD.main_concern: Novelty and controls are questioned: it combines DP2-style second-moment preconditioning with SlaClip, lacks preconditioned flat-clipping and DP2 baselines, and its experiments use a rank-1 Kronecker approximation of the stated preconditioner that appears only in the appendix.

mNtBkOWBl9.one_liner: Denoiser-based diffusion for discrete ordinal data with bidirectional (up and down) count perturbations.
mNtBkOWBl9.problem: Diffusion models for discrete integer-valued data such as images, music and gene counts are less developed than continuous diffusion or categorical discrete diffusion.
mNtBkOWBl9.method: Jumping Up and Down (JUD) defines two corruption processes, one that increases and one that depletes values, and reverses the joint process by modeling each noise separately with trained denoisers. Variants include Binomial-Poisson, Poisson-Poisson, up-only Poisson and down-only Binomial, trained with a simple cross-entropy-compatible objective.
mNtBkOWBl9.key_idea: Link latent conditional-mean denoisers to bidirectional reverse jump rates so a simple denoising loss trains both up- and down-jump corruptions of integer data.
mNtBkOWBl9.evidence: Experiments across data modalities including CIFAR-10 image generation and Sudoku, compared with discrete diffusion baselines and continuous EDM per reviewers.
mNtBkOWBl9.claimed_gains: Reports competitive results across different data modalities; the visible abstract gives no numbers, though a reviewer cites a CIFAR-10 FID of 2.07 for Binomial-Poisson.
mNtBkOWBl9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory simple and elegant, with an explicit link between denoising losses and bidirectional reverse jump rates, and strong CIFAR-10 results among discrete diffusion models.
mNtBkOWBl9.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate the benefit of bidirectional corruption (no matched Binomial-only model with the same backbone, preconditioning and training budget), and no experiment uses tasks where ordinality matters, such as gene counts or MIDI.

LTJHr87kUD.one_liner: Uses Muon's matrix updates for joint batch acquisition optimization in Bayesian optimization, with curvature and regret analysis.
LTJHr87kUD.problem: Batch Bayesian optimization selects candidates with dependent outcomes, so joint acquisition optimization needs coordinated updates, and it is unclear when matrix-based updates help.
LTJHr87kUD.method: Represents the batch as a matrix, relates posterior dependence to gradient modes, and for radial kernels characterizes single-point EI and chained batch-UCB curvature through a shared metric with rank-bounded corrections. It derives an exact local comparison identifying when Muon's normalization of active singular modes improves quadratic gain, motivating Muon-BO, plus a regret bound with explicit acquisition-optimization error.
LTJHr87kUD.key_idea: Treat the batch as a matrix and apply Muon's normalization of active singular modes when acquisition curvature makes it improve the local quadratic gain.
LTJHr87kUD.evidence: Theory plus experiments on GP draws, synthetic benchmarks (Ackley, Levy, Rastrigin) and a rover task, using a custom NumPy and SciPy implementation per reviewers.
LTJHr87kUD.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says experiments demonstrate practical benefits without numbers.
LTJHr87kUD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find applying Muon to acquisition optimization timely and natural, cheap and simple to implement, with theory giving intuition and experiments showing improved batch BO over other inner solvers.
LTJHr87kUD.main_concern: The theory does not clearly explain the empirical gains (key conditions are unchecked on real runs and cumulative regret is similar across inner optimizers), and experiments are mostly noiseless with a custom implementation and no BoTorch baseline.

bkwlR0ND2g.one_liner: Associative memory for test-time adaptation that recalls shared parameter-adjustment directions via a visual style descriptor.
bkwlR0ND2g.problem: Test-time adaptation must handle conditions that disappear and return, but updating a single model overwrites useful adaptations and test-time mixtures of experts need separate parameter states and input-dependent routing.
bkwlR0ND2g.method: ENGRAM is a plug-in memory: for each test batch a visual style descriptor retrieves a linear combination of shared parameter-adjustment directions learned online. After adaptation an error-correcting write updates the memory and a compensating residual retains adjustments the read has not yet reproduced, preserving the adapted parameters exactly.
bkwlR0ND2g.key_idea: Store shared parameter-update directions in a key-addressed linear memory with error-correcting writes and a compensating residual, so recalling past conditions needs no per-condition expert.
bkwlR0ND2g.evidence: ImageNet-C, CIFAR-10/100-C, DomainNet-126, PACS and Cityscapes-to-ACDC segmentation under recurring and evolving shifts, with CNNs, ViTs, LoRA and prompt tuning, plus a bound on parameter error when conditions return.
bkwlR0ND2g.claimed_gains: Improves over matched expert-based baselines in 26 of 30 comparisons, attains the lowest final error in all six settings including 27.2% on CIFAR-100-C, and improves ACDC segmentation by 2.7 mIoU points with LoRA.
bkwlR0ND2g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of retrieving adjustments from a shared memory instead of keeping one expert per domain clear and technically motivated, with broad experiments, informative ablations and a cost analysis.
bkwlR0ND2g.main_concern: Comparisons may not be matched: many baseline numbers come from published results while ENGRAM rows are newly measured, memory budgets are not matched in storage, and recall depends on descriptor quality with possible interference between similar conditions.

NcNOzjAlaf.one_liner: Identifiable second-moment geometry of dynamic network embeddings giving global and mode-wise trajectories, node attribution and change points.
NcNOzjAlaf.problem: Unfolded spectral embeddings of dynamic networks are invariant to general linear transformations that preserve edge probabilities but distort Euclidean second moments, so distances and directions of change are not identifiable.
NcNOzjAlaf.method: MENT takes pairwise second-moment operators of dynamic latent positions as estimands, identifiable up to simultaneous orthogonal conjugation under an isotropic normalization of shared anchor positions. They give a global trace variation distance that decomposes exactly across shared orthogonal modes, classical MDS turns distances into trajectories, and a modified unfolded spectral estimator consistently recovers them.
NcNOzjAlaf.key_idea: Impose isotropy on shared anchor latent positions so second-moment operators become identifiable up to rotation, giving distances that decompose exactly across shared orthogonal modes.
NcNOzjAlaf.evidence: Consistency, node-attribution and change-point localization bounds, with synthetic experiments validating geometric recovery and real-world case studies (abstract truncated).
NcNOzjAlaf.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says synthetic experiments show improved detection but is cut off before any numbers.
NcNOzjAlaf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem of interpreting unfolded spectral geometry real and the operator-to-distance-to-trajectory construction principled, with an exact decomposition of global distance into mode-wise distances.
NcNOzjAlaf.main_concern: Positioning and novelty are questioned: the procedure may coincide with Intensity Profile Projection, related identifiability work (simplex, NMF, mixed-membership) is not cited, and the change-point theorem does not cover the multiple-change-point procedure used in experiments.

uKcwiYGjeM.one_liner: Fits local Gaussian mixtures per input, aligns components across inputs, and smooths each with a heteroscedastic GP.
uKcwiYGjeM.problem: Gaussian processes give Gaussian predictive distributions that cannot represent multimodal or strongly non-Gaussian outputs, and exact inference in a fully coupled mixture-of-GPs model is exponentially intractable.
uKcwiYGjeM.method: GGMP fits local Gaussian mixtures at each input from repeated-measure data, aligns components across inputs, and trains one heteroscedastic GP per component, giving a closed-form Gaussian mixture predictive density compatible with standard and scalable GP solvers. It proves alignment recovers the true component correspondence under separation, smoothness, accurate local fits and dense inputs, and shows when component collisions make it unrecoverable.
uKcwiYGjeM.key_idea: Decouple the mixture-of-GPs into local mixture fits, component alignment across inputs, and one heteroscedastic GP per component, with alignment proven correct under component separation.
uKcwiYGjeM.evidence: Synthetic and real-world repeated-measure datasets (temperature and additive-manufacturing data per reviewers) compared with neural and random-forest conditional density estimators, with controlled ablations.
uKcwiYGjeM.claimed_gains: Competitive with neural and random-forest conditional density estimators on synthetic and real-world repeated-measure datasets; no numbers stated.
uKcwiYGjeM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory (alignment recovery, non-identifiability at collisions, consistency) strong and self-consistent, with carefully designed ablations and a useful scalable training pattern for GP mixtures.
uKcwiYGjeM.main_concern: Experiments do not show a broad advantage: mixture density networks match or beat GGMP on several metrics, comparisons are not matched in data exposure or hardware, and only exact GPs are used despite the scalability claim.

aFYfsGf69Z.one_liner: Shows learned multiview 3D-consistency metrics are fooled by hallucinated geometry and proposes COLMAP-based metrics.
aFYfsGf69Z.problem: Neural multiview consistency metrics such as MEt3R can score inconsistent image sets, even random noise, as near perfectly consistent and disagree with human judgments on novel view synthesis.
aFYfsGf69Z.method: SysCON3D is a controlled robustness benchmark that isolates 3D inconsistency, and the authors decompose reconstruction-based neural metrics into backbone, residual and aggregation components. Because feed-forward backbones hallucinate geometry, they introduce COLMAP-based metrics (including W-GPC) that use verified matches, camera registration, dense support and reconstruction failure as evaluation signals.
aFYfsGf69Z.key_idea: Replace feed-forward reconstruction backbones with COLMAP geometric verification, so unsupported views fail to register or match instead of being hallucinated into consistency.
aFYfsGf69Z.evidence: Controlled corruption tests on nine Mip-NeRF360 scenes with five inconsistency types across VGGT, MASt3R, DUSt3R and Fast3R backbones, and human-alignment studies on novel view synthesis outputs.
aFYfsGf69Z.claimed_gains: The best neural variant is about 3x more robust than MEt3R on SysCON3D, and the COLMAP-based metrics achieve the strongest human alignment of all metrics in the experiments.
aFYfsGf69Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper exposes a consequential failure of learned consistency metrics, with controlled experiments across several backbones and a useful diagnostic decomposition, and that the COLMAP metrics align well with human judgments.
aFYfsGf69Z.main_concern: Metric validity is not fully established: angular coverage alone correlates with human rankings nearly as well as W-GPC, human scores mix consistency with realism and plausibility, and the benchmark covers few scenes and conditions.

UzCzdIOfVc.one_liner: Uses a world action model's predicted video as targets for an action refiner, then fine-tunes on refined rollouts.
UzCzdIOfVc.problem: World action models predict plausible video outcomes that their generated actions fail to realize, because the action branch has far less paired supervision than the video branch.
UzCzdIOfVc.method: A lightweight refiner trained only on the original demonstrations corrects local execution deviations using predicted visual outcomes as targets. Selectively aggregated rollout data is combined with the original demonstrations to fine-tune the WAM, and the loop repeats over several rounds without new human demonstrations or an expert.
UzCzdIOfVc.key_idea: Treat the WAM's own predicted video as the target for a refiner that corrects executed actions, and distill the corrected rollouts back into the WAM.
UzCzdIOfVc.evidence: Evaluated on LIBERO, an adapted LIBERO-plus benchmark with three self-improvement rounds, and real-world robot experiments.
UzCzdIOfVc.claimed_gains: On LIBERO, fine-tuning raises FastWAM-joint's average success rate from 97.3% to 97.9% without the refiner; the LIBERO-plus numbers are cut off in the supplied abstract.
UzCzdIOfVc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like that the model improves from environment interaction without extra human corrections or expert demonstrations, and that the pipeline is clearly structured and evaluated in simulation and on real robots.
UzCzdIOfVc.main_concern: Predicted videos may be inaccurate or infeasible so the refiner can be steered to wrong targets, and gains on saturated LIBERO (97.3 to 97.9) are marginal with limited external baselines.

eFuG7pSeey.one_liner: Picks denoising steps from one trajectory whose distribution matches many generations (MMD), enabling cheap semantic uncertainty estimates.
eFuG7pSeey.problem: Sampling-based semantic uncertainty quantification for large language diffusion models needs many independent generations, which is expensive.
eFuG7pSeey.method: DiMS learns which diffusion steps of a single denoising trajectory to use, by minimizing a convex MMD-based objective derived from a decomposition of the single-trajectory approximation error into distribution mismatch and within-trajectory redundancy. It needs only a small unlabeled calibration set and plugs into existing semantic UQ estimators.
eFuG7pSeey.key_idea: Choose intermediate denoising states by matching their distribution (MMD) to that of independent generations, instead of sampling multiple trajectories.
eFuG7pSeey.evidence: Tested across three LLDMs, six datasets and eight semantic UQ estimators, with a timing comparison against 20 reference generations.
eFuG7pSeey.claimed_gains: Best or tied for best among single-trajectory strategies in 34/40 settings; cuts average per-prompt overhead from 66.8 s to 3.5 s versus 20 sequentially decoded generations, and 20 batched generations still take 5.9 times as long as one trajectory.
eFuG7pSeey.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value using intermediate answers from the denoising process to cut UQ cost, and that the method needs no change to the diffusion LLM and works with any semantic estimator.
eFuG7pSeey.main_concern: Improvements are modest (average AUROC 0.655 vs 0.643 for Full and 0.636 for Random) with a large gap to 20 i.i.d. generations (0.709), and simple baselines such as uniform or early-late stratified step selection are missing.

QHDCSKBDL8.one_liner: Negates the predicted velocity during early sampling steps of flow-matching models to raise sample diversity without training.
QHDCSKBDL8.problem: Flow-matching models such as FLUX concentrate samples around a few modes, and existing diversity methods need joint sampling, extra computation, or text-embedding and CFG manipulation.
QHDCSKBDL8.method: Training-free: the predicted velocity field is reversed in the early sampling steps. The authors support this with an analysis of how scaling a velocity field changes differential entropy.
QHDCSKBDL8.key_idea: Reversing a contractive velocity field in early steps increases entropy and pushes trajectories toward low-density regions, which widens mode coverage.
QHDCSKBDL8.evidence: Applied to image (FLUX, Z-Image Turbo), video (LTX) and 3D (TRELLIS) generators, with GenEval diversity results compared against noise-initialization, batch-interaction and guidance-based methods.
QHDCSKBDL8.claimed_gains: On GenEval it exceeds the diversity range of noise-initialization methods and rivals batch-interaction methods without joint sampling; the guidance-method comparison is cut off in the supplied abstract and no numbers are given.
QHDCSKBDL8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a simple, one-line, model-agnostic inference-time method with negligible overhead and a broad evaluation across models, baselines and quality metrics.
QHDCSKBDL8.main_concern: The entropy argument does not establish improved mode coverage and the ablations do not isolate velocity inversion from other changes such as noise-norm inflation.

84mRWpUKkf.one_liner: Greedily prunes MLP neurons by the reconstruction error left after optimal affine compensation, rather than by a fixed importance score.
84mRWpUKkf.problem: Post-training structured pruning ranks neurons by importance before compensation, ignoring what can be recovered by the surviving neurons.
84mRWpUKkf.method: CARVE greedily removes the neuron whose removal least increases reconstruction error after optimal affine compensation through the remaining neurons, updating compensated weights and the precision matrix in closed form. A global allocation strategy rescales local errors by the residual-stream signal to compare blocks.
84mRWpUKkf.key_idea: Select neurons to prune by the exact error remaining after optimal compensation, recomputed as the surviving set changes.
84mRWpUKkf.evidence: ImageNet-1k with nine vision backbones from 5.7M to 632M parameters and nine MLP sparsities from 10% to 90%, without fine-tuning; reviews also mention perplexity tests on Qwen.
84mRWpUKkf.claimed_gains: not stated (the supplied abstract is cut off after 'Without fine-tuning, CARVE outperforms the').
84mRWpUKkf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the closed-form selection and compensation framing intuitive, the experiments broad across backbones and sparsities, and the theory and writing solid.
84mRWpUKkf.main_concern: Novelty relative to OBS and OBC is unclear, and results are mostly on ImageNet with only perplexity tested on the language model.

2RNwqA5h3s.one_liner: Verifies candidate action chunks of flow-matching VLAs with a learned temporal token and an energy-based verifier.
2RNwqA5h3s.problem: Existing test-time action verification for generative robot policies is temporally myopic, scoring candidates from the current observation only, and often needs large verifiers and extra expert demonstrations.
2RNwqA5h3s.method: TeV learns a temporal token summarizing recent observation-action history so candidates are scored as continuations of the trajectory. Conditioned on this token, it builds positive-negative pairs without extra expert demonstrations or preference annotations and trains an energy-based verifier (the abstract is cut off after this).
2RNwqA5h3s.key_idea: Condition an energy-based action verifier on a learned history token so candidate chunks are judged for trajectory continuity.
2RNwqA5h3s.evidence: Simulation and real-world robot experiments with the same VLA backbone, compared against LPB, DynaGuide, FOREWARN and TACO, with ablations on negative-example strategy, guidance and verification.
2RNwqA5h3s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea sensible and clearly written, with complete experiments in simulation and the real world, thorough ablations, and reuse of existing demonstrations with small added modules.
2RNwqA5h3s.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate history from verification (no current-frame verifier), and baseline training details and high real-world variance make comparisons hard to interpret.

jRJJKlciJo.one_liner: Distills sequence-level power-distribution sampling into a model using on-policy sequential Monte Carlo and weighted maximum likelihood.
jRJJKlciJo.problem: Power-distribution sampling improves reasoning accuracy but needs many candidate answers per query at inference time.
jRJJKlciJo.method: On-policy power distillation (OPPD) runs a sequential Monte Carlo sampler in which the model being trained generates candidates and a frozen teacher's power distribution weights them. The same teacher probabilities give each full answer a weight for weighted maximum likelihood.
jRJJKlciJo.key_idea: Move the cost of power-distribution sharpening into training by weighting on-policy SMC samples with the teacher's power distribution.
jRJJKlciJo.evidence: Qwen2.5-Math-7B evaluated on MATH500 and GSM8K against the untrained model and published power sampling with 64 candidates.
jRJJKlciJo.claimed_gains: On Qwen2.5-Math-7B, single-generation accuracy rises 21.7 points on MATH500 and 26.5 on GSM8K at the same temperature, and one generation scores 3.3 points above published power sampling with 64 candidates on both benchmarks; the MATH500 comparison with the authors' own sampler is cut off.
jRJJKlciJo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the gains substantial and the idea of shifting sampling cost to label-free training natural, with gains beyond temperature changes and transfer from GSM8K-like training to MATH500.
jRJJKlciJo.main_concern: The blockwise training-weight reset in the implementation does not clearly match the sequence-level objective used in the theory, and comparison with simpler sharpening methods is missing.

jQkjbGFLav.one_liner: Attaches a conditional normalizing flow head to an autoregressive language model to predict the next continuous vector.
jQkjbGFLav.problem: Extending next-token prediction to continuous signals such as images and robot actions is hard because they are vectors rather than discrete tokens.
jQkjbGFLav.method: AutoFlow equips a language model with a conditional normalizing flow that predicts the next continuous vector, leaving the autoregressive backbone unchanged. It generates continuous outputs in one forward evaluation and returns their likelihood directly.
jQkjbGFLav.key_idea: Replace diffusion heads with an exact-likelihood conditional normalizing flow on clean targets as the continuous output interface of an autoregressive model.
jQkjbGFLav.evidence: Image generation, transfer from image generation to visual understanding, interleaved image-text reasoning and robot action prediction, compared with diffusion-based heads.
